en: The Scripture of the Great King of Teachings of the Supreme Root Mahāsukha Vajra Amoghasamādhi, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Great Master Mingjiao, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Ritual Manual on the True Principle of the Great Samaya Vajra. Thus have I heard:

At one time, the World-Honored One, the Buddha Mahāvairocana, was dwelling in the palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven. That celestial palace was composed of various jewels and adorned with suspended bells, necklaces, banners, pennants, pearls, gems, and all manner of precious canopies; thus arrayed, these ornaments filled the entirety of space.

This Buddha, the World-Honored One, dwells securely in the wisdom of the vajra-samādhi of all Buddhas, the most venerable among the holy ones; he wears the crown of all Buddhas and has received the consecration of the Dharma King of the triple world; he has accomplished the omniscient wisdom of all Buddhas and is the most perfectly corresponding, sovereign, and unimpeded one; he possesses the seal of equality of all Buddhas and is skilled in performing various activities; he fulfills all vows throughout the entire realm of sentient beings; he is the ultimate Dharmakāya, equal to the triple world; he encompasses the vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, and is praised by all Buddhas.
This Great Compassionate One, the Great Vairocana Tathāgata, was accompanied by eight koṭis of great bodhisattvas, whose names were:

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagandha, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvamāradharṣaka. Surrounded by such a multitude of great bodhisattvas, he proclaimed all the gateways to the pure Dharma—excellent in the beginning, middle, and end; profound in both word and meaning; pure and unadulterated; complete and perfect.
That is to say:
the phrase "purity of sublime bliss" is itself the phrase "enlightenment";
the phrase "purity of sensual desire" is itself the phrase "enlightenment."
The phrase "purity through intimacy with the Dharma" is itself the phrase of bodhi;
the phrase "purity of all wealth and happiness" is itself the phrase of bodhi;
the phrase "purity of vision" is itself the phrase of bodhi.
The phrase "purity of delight" is itself the phrase of bodhi;
the phrase "purity of defiled phenomena" is itself the phrase of bodhi;
the phrase "purity of adornment" is itself the phrase of bodhi.
The phrase "purity of delight" is itself the phrase of bodhi;
the phrase "purity of luminous illumination" is itself the phrase of bodhi;
the phrase "purity of body" is itself the phrase of bodhi.
The phrase "purity of form" is itself the phrase "enlightenment";
the phrase "purity of sound" is itself the phrase "enlightenment";
the phrase "purity of fragrance" is itself the phrase "enlightenment."
The phrase "purity of taste" is itself the phrase "enlightenment";
the phrase "purity of touch" is itself the phrase "enlightenment. Why is this so?
The intrinsic purity of all phenomena is likewise so.
Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is also pure.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:

“If any person hears this Prajñāpāramitā, the Dharma-gate of Universal Purity, that person shall immediately eliminate all hindrances—namely, the hindrance of afflictions (*kleśāvaraṇa*), the hindrance of phenomena (*dharmāvaraṇa*), and the hindrance of karma (*karmāvaraṇa*).

All factors that obstruct the Path shall be utterly extinguished; even if they have created karma for the hells, they shall no longer experience its results. All suffering and distress shall be extinguished without remainder in a single instant, and they will swiftly reach the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*)."

If a person upholds, recites, memorizes, and contemplates this, that person will, in the present life, attain the samādhi of the equality of all dharmas, achieve mastery over all dharmas, obtain all cherished joys and satisfactions, and after passing through sixteen births as great bodhisattvas, attain perfect enlightenment.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Buddha, wishing to cause [Vajrapāṇi] to proclaim the supreme Mahāyāna samādhi-dharma of all Buddhas, the supreme dharmas of all maṇḍalas such as the Vajradhātu, the most excellent dharma for all sentient beings, the dharma of taming the exhaustible and the inexhaustible, the dharma of accomplishing all purposes, the great samādhi-dharma of Vajrapāṇi, and the immeasurable, secret, and wondrous dharmas.
Such dharmas as these constitute the pure dharma-gate of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, the Buddha Mahāvairocana first manifested a smile; with his left hand making a raised gesture, he playfully tossed a vajra.

Furthermore, forming the gesture of summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*) with the vajra and placing it at one’s own heart, one recites the *vidyā* of the Samādhi of the True Principle of the Heart of Great Bliss-Amogha-Vajra:

“HŪṂ. When this *vidyā* is recited, all Buddha-fields within the three realms, as well as all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, become entirely delighted and joyful; they are summoned into the great maṇḍala of the Buddha Mahāvairocana, abide in the Buddha-samādhi, and all become objects of veneration and love. All methods of accomplishment (*siddhi*) are thereby brought to fulfillment.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Buddha Mahāvairocana, having bound the seal of the Great Bliss Vajra, immediately entered the samādhi of the Secret Vajra of All Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Now you shall proclaim the maṇḍala rite.
At that time, having received the Buddha’s command, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi entered the samādhi of the Great Secret Vajra Samaya-born Maṇḍala Arrayed with the Wisdom Seal (jñānamudrā).
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he taught the method for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra-Abiding Contemplation on the True Principle of the Great Samādhi.
He then spoke these verses:
"Now, in accordance with the Buddha’s intent, I shall briefly explain the maṇḍala."
The true principle of samādhi is the visualization of the vajra-abiding;
with four gates and four corner towers adorned with jewels,
the maṇḍala is surrounded by the blazing light of the *vitasti*.
At the four corners and on the left and right of the gates, place the forms of half-moons.
Adorned with various jewels, they are hung with bells, pearl necklaces, precious canopies,
banners and streamers, bright mirrors, and clusters of flowers.
In the outer maṇḍala,
arrange the positions of the eight deities; in the central position is Vajrapāṇi,
who is named Vajracakra.
According to the ritual, install the honored image; its lunar color and lunar form radiate a blazing light that shines everywhere.
Holding a vajra in his hand, he manifests a posture of loftily raised [triumph], seated upon a lotus throne.
Surrounded by a perimeter of vajras, blazing with intense flames,
one holds the heart-mantra of the principal deity and visualizes the maṇḍala,
including all the worthy sages, while likewise holding their respective heart-mantras.
Arising from the Vajra, place images of jewels and painted icons surrounding the central deity;
install Vajrasattva, whose physical form is white with red hues.
Wearing the crown of all Buddhas upon his head, holding a vajra in his hand,
he manifests the posture of great summoning.
The Honored One Kilikīla is in color like Mahāvairocana.
His body is adorned with various jewels;
one should contemplate the Great Honored One Vajra, whose body is blue-white in color and who holds a makara banner in his hand.
The Great Honored One Vajramuṣṭi has a body the color of purple gold, with both hands in the vajra-fist mudrā.
In the four corners reside four honored ones, each holding a flower emblem: the lotus bowl and the uṣṇīṣa.
In the corners of the outer maṇḍala, place the *nīpakaṇṭha* [deities];
at each of the four gates and in their respective centers, place either images or emblems.
In the positions of the inner maṇḍala, place Vajrapāṇi and the others.
Extending to the very limits of the vajra-circle, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
fill it completely. Furthermore, in the outer maṇḍala, one should place the hosts of devas of the desire realm,
with the lords of the three realms— namely Śakra, Brahmā, and Maheśvara— positioned at the front.
Following such rituals as these, perform the maṇḍala rite.
Furthermore, the procedure for entering the maṇḍala is explained:
one should select [the site] according to the dharma, and this great Vajrācārya shall enter the ritual enclosure (maṇḍala).

Now, an ācārya must be proficient in all maṇḍala rituals, know all samādhi dharmas, and be well-versed in the characteristics of all phenomena. He must be capable of accomplishing all ritual procedures, constantly visualize himself as Vajrapāṇi, and have received all empowerment rites (*abhiṣeka*). He must master all-encompassing wisdom, understand the various matters of offering, and be skilled in the worldly and transworldly maṇḍala methods. Having perfected all secret mudrās, he achieves success in every seal he binds.

Even if there should be errors or transgressions, they will always manifest within the state of samādhi; without receiving instruction from a teacher, one understands them spontaneously, and all offerings are made accordingly.
These various signs mentioned above are now briefly explained.

"If a Vajrācārya seeks whatever supreme methods of accomplishment desired by the mind, they shall all be attained in this very life; even [the state of] a Bodhisattva and the knowledge of omniscience can all be accomplished."

Why is this? Because this great ācārya visualizes the Venerable Vajrapāṇi as ever residing within his own heart; furthermore, he summons him from that heart into the maṇḍala, where he abides in samādhi with joy and delight.
Once one has perfected oneself, one summons [the deity] into the maṇḍala; manifesting love and reverence, all that is undertaken is accomplished.

At that time, the ācārya, having bound the vajra-mudrā and performed the vajra-visualization, constantly recites the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) and performs the rite for the accomplishment of the great maṇḍala. Subsequently, he binds the vajra-lāsyā-mudrā and, while reciting the heart-mantra, assumes the posture of prostration.

The Ācārya must first purify himself, don red robes, and adorn himself with various ornaments; forming the vajra-anjali mudrā and assuming the posture of the vajra dance, he should hold incense and flowers and enter the maṇḍala with a composed mind.

Furthermore, while performing playful gestures and reciting the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*), one should then gaze upon Vajrapāṇi with the vajra-vision, take one's seat, and seek the accomplishment of Vajrapāṇi according to the ritual procedure.

At that time, Vajrapāṇi manifested a sign of auspiciousness through great joy; his brow slightly quivered, his entire body became crimson, a great radiance issued from his face, and he further displayed various supernatural powers.
Having manifested these supernatural powers, he then manifests his true body to bestow the supreme accomplishment.
From this point forward, one shall attain the accomplishment of all dharmas day by day.

Whether sitting or walking, this person cannot be seen by the gods; they are not subject to any prohibitions, are fully endowed with all accomplishments, obtain all wealth and happiness, and penetrate unsurpassed wisdom.
Vajrapāṇi brings all such matters to fulfillment.
Thereafter, one performs the worship oneself.
Having performed the worship, one receives empowerment for oneself through the rite of Vajra Empowerment.
Next, one should visualize and supplicate the vajra of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Once the supplication has been made, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi will immediately manifest his own form and personally bestow it upon the practitioner.
If this ācārya holds this vajra and seeks the most supreme accomplishments, he shall obtain them all within a single kṣaṇa.

If one holds the vajra oneself and performs recitation for the sake of the most supreme accomplishment, one will attain accomplishment after six months; thereafter, one likewise receives the vajra-abhiseka as previously described, and immediately performs offerings according to whatever one desires.
One should always maintain this great maṇḍala sādhanavidhi according to this ritual procedure.
Furthermore, the ritual for the disciple’s entry into the maṇḍala is proclaimed as follows.

The Vajrajñāna Ācārya must first form the mudrā of the Samādhi of the Vajra of Wondrous Bliss, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala to perform prostrations and pay homage, and cause them to contemplate whatever they seek or aspire to attain.

When seeking the method for the accomplishment of Vajrapāṇi, one should form the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and perform the rite of accomplishment; upon seeing its auspicious signs, all methods of accomplishment will be brought to fulfillment.

Once the disciple has thus entered the maṇḍala, the accomplishments they attain are no different from those of the ācārya. Thereafter, as before, they hold the vajra; such a person is called a "Vajra-disciple."
One shall then receive the Dharma of the Seals, the Dharma of the Samādhis of all Buddhas, and enter the Dharma of the various Worthies and Sages.

At that time, one should provide various offerings, producing celestial foods and the like, and enter the maṇḍala to present such offerings according to one's capacity, as well as offering playful garlands, song, and dance. According to the ritual, one should remain awake day and night, focusing the mind with single-minded devotion to seek the accomplishment of the Dharma. Arousing a mind of equanimity and making great vows, one should universally act for the sake of all sentient beings so that they may realize Bodhi.
Furthermore, he proclaimed the *sādhana* of Vajrapāṇi:

"The practitioner should begin on the fifteenth day before the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, form the Mudrā of the Wondrous Joyful Vajra (*Sukhavajra*), establish the boundary according to their wish, and recite with the Vajra-speech for one month until they attain proficiency."
From this point forward, all rites of accomplishment performed shall be successful, according to the true words of Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the practitioner, following the ritual manual, shall fashion an image; according to the maṇḍala rite, one should paint the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and the eight great Bodhisattvas.
Before the painted image, the practitioner begins on the fifteenth day;

first, they bind the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and recite the mantra with thorough mastery. For fifteen full days and nights, they do not release the seal, maintaining the recitation continuously so that the mind does not waver for even a single moment.

When the following morning arrived, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva manifested his true form, displaying a great smile; his body was like the color of the moon as he stood before the practitioner and granted their requested aspirations.
"Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is taught:

within the mandala, one should paint the Buddha Bhagavān, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, and the eight great bodhisattvas; surrounding them, one should further paint all the Tathāgatas. By reciting the mantra according to the previous ritual procedure, one will immediately attain all accomplishments."
Furthermore, within the mandala, one should depict the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi with exquisite incense and colors.

Before the image in the mandala, the practitioner should bind the mudrā and perform recitation for one hundred thousand (lakṣa) times. Once the count is complete, the practitioner immediately becomes Vajrasattva.

"Furthermore, according to the ritual procedure as before, if one merely paints the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and performs the recitation, one will immediately attain the accomplishment of the Buddha.
Moreover, if the practitioner enters the maṇḍala and performs the recitation therein, all wishes and aspirations shall be fully accomplished."

Furthermore, if the practitioner recites the root heart-mantra according to the ritual, all devas and humans will love and respect them. Once the recitation has reached one hundred thousand (*lakṣa*), their own person will receive protection. By consecrating white mustard seeds and giving them to others as a rite of protection, or by consecrating a vajra and rotating it, all people will immediately receive protection.

"Furthermore, there is another method: perform the visualization as in the previous maṇḍala visualization, form the mudrā, manifest the vajra-gaze, and likewise use mustard seeds to cause all hosts of māras to be bound."
"If one performs the recitation while not exhaling the breath, all demons and delusions will be completely subdued.
If one performs the recitation according to the adamantine and firm method, all shall be summoned."
"If one recites while closing the eyes, all hosts of māras will naturally be extinguished.
If one recites while forming the Vajra-Chain mudrā, all hosts of māras will be completely sealed by it."
"If one binds the Vajra-Ḍākinī mudrā and performs the recitation, one summons the hearts of all māras.
If one recites with speed, the hosts of māras will all be struck with fear."
"If one binds the Vajrapāṇi mudrā and performs recitation, all aims will be accomplished.
If one desires to seek great wealth and treasures, one should bind the Vajrayoginī mudrā."
"If one wishes for all sentient beings to be satisfied and joyful, one should perform recitation with a subtle and wondrous voice; then all sentient beings will attain satisfaction and joy."
"If one seeks to inspire joy, love, and reverence in the Buddhas and Tathāgatas of the ten directions, one should form the Vajra-Arrow mudrā and recite the heart-mantra.
If one desires to make one's intimacy firm and enduring, one should form the Firm Fist mudrā, place it at one's own heart, and recite."
"If one wishes to resolve all anger and resentment, one should form the 'Highly Exalted' gesture (*udvṛtta-mudrā*) and perform the recitation.
If one wishes for sentient beings to be pleased, one should place the vajra-fist at the heart and perform the recitation."
"If one wishes to dispel darkness, one should face east and rotate the vajra-wheel.
If one wishes for physical well-being, one should consecrate one's own body."
"If one wishes to manifest various forms and images, one should bind the Vajra-form Seal (Vajrarūpamudrā).
If one wishes to hear various sounds, one should empower the Vajra-lute."
"If one wishes to hear various sublime fragrances, one should visualize the empowerment of fragrance.
If one wishes to perceive the most excellent flavors, one should empower the vajra."
"If one wishes to perform the rite of entering and awakening, one should empower both hands and either clap them together or snap the fingers.
If one wishes to release all malevolent planets (grahas), one should form the Vajramudgara mudrā."
"If one wishes to cause the various stellar deities (grahas) to become possessed [by the mantra], one should assume a wrathful expression before an image of the deity Vināyaka and recite it aloud."
"If one wishes to dispel various malignant diseases, one should manifest the Vajra-gaze.
If one wishes to dispel various poisons, one should employ the Peacock Whisk.
If one wishes to dispel various toxic drugs, one should employ the Amṛta Seal."
"If one wishes to eliminate all evil māras, one should manifest a wrathful demeanor and recite [the mantra] continuously without interruption.
If one wishes to dispel all malevolent spirits, one should employ the Vajra-Playful-Throw mudrā."
"If one wishes to shatter all evil mudrās, one should assume the posture of wrath.
If one wishes to summon all ḍākinīs, one should employ the Vajrakhaṭvāṅga mudrā."
If one wishes to destroy the mātaras, the maṇḍala-demons, and the various heterodox samaya-mantras, one should employ the dust from beneath the feet of the Vajra-krodha-rāja.
"If one wishes to cause the various ghosts and spirits to serve as attendants, one should manifest a form of great wrath within a shrine and recite the mantra.
If one wishes to subdue the armies of Māra, one should manifest the form of the Great Wrathful Vajra and further manifest a form of great laughter."
"If one wishes to break the enemy's army, one should empower a vajra and hurl it.
If one wishes to enter a military array seeking victory, one should employ the Vajrakīṭa mudrā."
"If one wishes to perform binding, one should use empowered clothing to tie [the person];
if one wishes to release them, one should recite their name.
If one wishes to destroy the city of the Vetāla ghosts, one should employ the Vajrapañjara mudrā."
"If one wishes to loosen all fetters and shackles, one should employ the Vajraprokṣa mudrā.
If one wishes to produce fire, one should consecrate the Vajrasūryamaṇi."
"If one wishes to cause water to emerge from a parched place, one should empower the *vajracandrakānta* jewel.
If one wishes to seek various kinds of food, drink, clothing, and so forth, one should gaze into the void and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*)."
"If you wish to see all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas pervading space, you must recollect the Buddhas and maintain the recitation with single-minded concentration.

If you wish for the appearance of the form of syllables in the sky to perceive the events of the three periods of time, you should write the letter 'A' and recite it one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*); then you will immediately see the affairs of the three periods."
Just as the eye perceives what it sees, so too is it with the mind’s cognition of mental objects (*dharmas*).
If one empowers the eye with one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣa*), one will be able to perceive the forms and images of the three periods of time;
if one empowers the ear, one will hear the sounds of the three periods of time.
If one empowers the nose, one can distinguish the fragrances of the three periods of time;
if one empowers the tongue, one can skillfully explain the events of the three periods of time;
if one empowers the mind, one can discern the true and wondrous principle.
"If one wishes to accomplish the forms of all Buddha-images and behold rare wonders, one should perform empowerment for one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣa*).
If one wishes to see illusory transformations, one should use a peacock-feather whisk."
"If one desires to obtain all requisites for enjoyment, one should go to a temple of Maheśvara and perform recitation one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*).
If one desires to see various sacred sites, one should employ the *Trailokyavijaya-mudrā*."
"If one wishes to accomplish all dharmas, one should employ the Vajra-jñāna-mudrā.
If one wishes to see the sages possessing the five supernatural powers, one should employ the Vajra-samādhi-mudrā."

"If one desires to personally achieve the fruit of Buddhahood or the stage of a Bodhisattva, and to manifest various deeds within the four modes of deportment, one should employ the Vajra-līlā-samaya-mudrā."
"If you wish to awaken the various devas, you should employ the Vajrabala-mudrā.
If you wish to subjugate the nāgas, you should go to a nāga pond and perform the recitation."
"If one wishes to cause the yakṣas to become servants, one should employ the Vajra-ādeśa-mudrā.
If one wishes to subdue the bhūtas, one should tread upon an image of Maheśvara with the feet, manifesting a great wrathful demeanor while reciting the heart-mantra."
"If one wishes to stop thunder and hail, one should employ the Vajratāvaṇa mudrā.
If one wishes to extinguish calamitous fires, one should employ the Bhṛkuṭī Bodhisattva mudrā."
"If you wish to cause rain to fall, you should go to a dragon pond and perform recitation.
If you wish to stop the rain, you should perform homa in water using withered flowers."
"If you wish to raise wind and clouds, you should draw the form of a dragon and fumigate it with incense.
If you wish to seek clear weather, you should employ the Vajra-Gaganagañja-Buddhalocanā Mudrā."
"If one wishes to cause springs to emerge from parched places, one should employ the Ultimate Vajra Nāga Seal.
If one wishes to manifest hidden treasures, one should employ the Vajra Khaṭvāṅga Seal."
"If one wishes to seek the various hidden treasures (*pātāla*), one should employ the Vajrārtha-mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish all maṇḍalas, one should employ the Vajracakra-mudrā."
"If one wishes to accomplish the dharmas of all mudrās, one should employ the Great Bliss Vajra Samādhi Mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish the dharmas of all samādhis, one should employ the Sublime Bliss Vajra Mudrā."
"If one wishes to accomplish the vidyādharas, one should employ the vajra-mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish the bodhisattvas of the Vajra Family, one should employ the supreme root vajra-mudrā."
"If one wishes to accomplish all bodhisattvas, one should employ the Vajra-mudrā of the Mind.
If one wishes to accomplish the Vajra-bodhisattvas, one should employ the Great Vajra-mudrā."
"If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of all Buddhas, one should employ the Vajra-jñāna-muṣṭi-mudrā.
As with all the aforementioned dharmas, they must all be empowered by the heart-mantra (citta-vidyā)."

Chapter Two: The Ritual Manual of the Vajra-Samādhi of the True Principle of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the Buddha Mahāvairocana again himself proclaimed this teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Dharma-gate of the Bodhi of all Buddhas.
That is to say:
because it is the awakening to the equality of the vajra, it is awakening;
because it is the awakening to the equality of the meaning of the firmness of the vajra, it is awakening.
Because it is the awakening to the equality of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), it is awakening;
because it is the awakening to the equality of all phenomena that are pure by nature (*prakṛtiviśuddha*), it is awakening.
The non-differentiation of all phenomena is likewise so.

If anyone hears, receives, upholds, reads, or recites these four Dharma-gates, all their obstacles will be completely extinguished, until they realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* at the site of enlightenment.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Buddha, having spoken this Dharma-gate of True Principle, again formed the Wisdom Fist, manifested a great smile, and spoke the Heart-Mantra of the Equality of All Dharmas.
It is said:

"ĀḤ" explains that in the midst of this heart-mantra (hṛdaya), all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas gather like clouds, surrounding the Great Vairocana Buddha and sitting in succession according to the positions of the Vajrasattva Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, there were eight great bodhisattvas seated in the eight directions of the outer maṇḍala, manifesting with great smiles.
At that time, the Buddha Mahāvairocana entered the samādhi called "The Mental Abiding in the Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he then proclaimed the Great Maṇḍala Dharma of the Vajra Reality Principle of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas:
"Following the ritual of the previous Vajrasattva Maṇḍala, one should construct the outer maṇḍala."
Within this maṇḍala, draw a vajra-wheel; within that wheel, draw a multi-colored lotus; upon that lotus, place the Blessed One, the Buddha.
Around the Blessed One, further place eight Buddhas, each seated upon a sun-disc and holding a vajra.

Furthermore, at the four cardinal and four intermediate corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should install the eight great bodhisattvas according to the ritual rules. At each of the four gates, place an *argha* vase; these vases must be selected according to the ritual rules, filled with scented water, and adorned within with exquisite flowers and fruits. Furthermore, place the five jewels, the five grains, and the five medicines inside the vases, and cover the top of each vase with fine colored silk.
Thereafter, having bound the vajra-mudrās of all the Buddhas and made offerings to them, one should then place the vases at the four gates.
At that time, the ācārya, visualizing his own body according to the ritual as being identical to the bodies of all the Buddhas, considers himself to have become a Vajra-ācārya.
From this point onward, one shall attain all accomplishments within the teachings of all Buddhas and eliminate all obstacles.
Thereafter, one causes the disciple to enter the maṇḍala and, according to the ritual, performs the consecration of the five places with a vajra; this is called the Vajra Consecration.
He then spoke this verse of the samaya-vow for this samādhi:
“Having received this empowerment, you shall universally act for the sake of all sentient beings,
increase all Buddha-dharmas, and abide in a mind of equanimity.”
"Then, according to their respective faculties and natures, one should act in accordance with the four types of insignia (cihna) as prescribed by the ritual.
Having thus explained this Samaya-maṇḍala, he further spoke on the method for accomplishing the painted image (paṭavidhāna):

"Within that painting, one should depict the Great Vairocana Buddha, radiant with light, his two hands forming the Wisdom Fist Mudrā (jñānamuṣṭi-mudrā) of all Buddhas; the remaining Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are all to be depicted according to the procedure of the previous maṇḍala."
Thereafter, before this mandala, perform the rites of accomplishment according to your inclination, and you shall obtain the supreme accomplishment.
Furthermore, the method for the painted image is explained:

within the mandala, depict only the Buddha Mahāvairocana. Before this mandala, recite the mantra according to your inclination; thereafter, form the Wisdom Fist Mudrā with both hands and recite throughout the night. One will then attain the accomplishment of Prajñāpāramitā, realize the stage of a Bodhisattva, and upon rebirth, immediately achieve Perfect Enlightenment.
The above has been explained for those who have already accomplished the maṇḍala;
now it shall be explained again for those who have not yet accomplished the maṇḍala.
"If you wish to receive the offerings of the Buddha, you should bestow all forms of happiness upon others.
If you wish to receive offerings as a Bodhisattva does, you should offer exquisite flowers to the Triple Gem and must also recite the heart-mantra."
"If you wish to cause all sentient beings to make offerings to you, you should recite with a mind of loving-kindness.
If you wish to encompass all dharmas, you should recite the four-line verse of the Prajñāpāramitā."
"If one wishes to subdue Māra, one should maintain the recitation with a mind firmly fixed in concentration.
If one wishes to seek the empowerment of all Buddhas, one should relinquish the ornaments that adorn one's own body."
"If one wishes to be fully endowed with all dharmas, one should employ the Vajrapadma-avalokana-mudrā.
If one wishes to seek the rites for the accomplishment of the *karma* of all Buddhas, one should employ the various Vajra-karma-mudrās."
"If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of all Buddhas, one should employ the Great Seal of the Vajra-Wisdom Fist.
As for the aforementioned dharmas, one must in all cases recite the heart-mantra."

The Great King of Tantras of the Supreme Root Mahāsukha Vajra Amoghasamādhi, translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Imperially Appointed Court Honorable Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Dharma-Bhadra, by Imperial Decree. Volume One. Part Three: The Great Ritual Manual of the Vajrasamādhi for Subjugating the Three Realms. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha spoke the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā, the most supreme synthesis of the equality of all phenomena.
That is to say:
"Because greed has no intrinsic nature, hatred also has no intrinsic nature;
because hatred has no intrinsic nature, delusion also has no intrinsic nature."
Because ignorance has no intrinsic nature, all phenomena also have no intrinsic nature;
because all phenomena have no intrinsic nature, the *prajñāpāramitā* also has no intrinsic nature.

If there is a person who hears, receives, upholds, recites, and memorizes this Dharma-gate of the *prajñāpāramitā*, even if that person has committed the karma of killing all sentient beings within the three realms, they shall no longer undergo its retribution, shall not fall into the evil destinies, and will swiftly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, having heard the Buddha’s teaching on this Dharma-gate of the True Principle, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva immediately manifested a face of frowning brows, sharp fangs, and a mixture of wrath and joy; standing upon a lotus flower in the posture of drawing a bow, he formed the Seal for Subjugating the Three Realms and recited the Heart Mantra.
It is said:

"HŪṂ. When this heart-mantra is recited, all the lords of the gods of the three realms, the lords of the three realms, and even Maheśvara are summoned by means of the hook and made to enter the maṇḍala; through the method of subjugation, they are all subdued, granted consolation, and caused to abide in samādhi.

He further manifested the form of a great wrathful deity; thereupon Maheśvara, the Lord of the Three Realms, and all his retinues, seeing Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva manifesting as a great wrathful deity to subjugate the three realms, were all struck with terror and cried out, saying:
"Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva!..."
"Protect us! We take refuge in the Buddha; we shall abide in samādhi by receiving the holy command of the Buddha.

When all the mātaras and others saw the Bodhisattva manifesting his wrathful form, they were all greatly terrified, distressed, and bewildered. All their heterodox vidyās and heterodox mudrās were utterly destroyed, and even the seizing influences of the planets and lunar mansions, as well as all diseases and poisons, were completely eliminated.
At that time, the various mātṛkās and others also raised their voices and said:
"O Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva!
Protect and deliver us!"
"From this day forward, we take refuge in the Buddha; we pray that you grant us your grace and empowerment.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva manifested a smile and led the devas and others into the maṇḍala, establishing them in samādhi and bestowing upon them the empowerment through the Ratnakula rite.
He further bestowed the empowerment through the Vajrakula rite, commanding them to bring great benefit to the entire realm of sentient beings and to abide within the outer Vajrakula.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi manifested as a Vidyārāja, assuming the appearance of a wrathful one who subdues the three realms. He was adorned with various ornaments and displayed great ferocity; his sharp fangs bit his lips, and his beard and hair stood erect and red. Holding a vajra, a hook, a sword, a staff, a *kṛpīṭa*, and other implements, this Great Vidyārāja dwelt according to the ritual procedures of the Vajrapāṇi Maṇḍala.
Those various devas are installed in the outer maṇḍala; outside this maṇḍala, the various nakṣatras and grahas are installed.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi entered the vajra-samādhi of the great compassion and skillful means of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he taught this ritual procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra of the Most Victorious Peaceful Perception that Subdues the Three Realms.
The verse says:
"I shall now briefly explain this most supreme maṇḍala."
Named "Subduer of the Three Realms," he is able to tame those who are difficult to tame.
Following the aforementioned ritual for expounding the Dharma, one should draw the outer maṇḍala;
within the inner wheel, the positions of the eight deities are arranged in their respective places.
In the center resides the Wrathful Lord, his body the color of a blue lotus, adorned with various ornaments.
With furrowed brows and protruding fangs, he wears a wrathful smile;
he stands in the posture of one drawing a bow.
This is the sign of subduing the three realms: beneath his two feet,
he tramples the Lord of the Heaven of Freedom with his left foot and the Queen of the Heaven of Freedom with his right,
while his blazing radiance shines everywhere.
Radiant light shines everywhere; following the previous ritual for the outer mandala, draw the outer maṇḍala.
[Depict] the form of a great wrathful deity, with bow, arrow, sword, and wheel.
These are the four insignia.
One should place the insignia of the various luminaries, various foods of superior flavor, and a full bowl as the source of production; one should then install a blue bell.
Together with various colored banners and streamers,
one should wear blue robes and manifest a wrathful expression;
then, forming the samaya-mudrā, one enters the maṇḍala.
The Ācārya must perform the Buddha-activities according to the Dharma;
from this day forward, the various devas shall be unable to see him.
He can accomplish or destroy all things and shall attain all that is most supreme.
May all methods of accomplishment bring about their fulfillment.
At that time, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala;
they shall form the vajra-mudrā and receive the vajra-abhiṣeka.
He then bestowed the vajra and conferred this vow:
"This vajra of Vajrapāṇi can subdue those who are difficult to subdue;
you should always uphold it and accomplish the supreme dharma."
"Having bestowed this vow, one emerges from the maṇḍala.
Having spoken these verses, he further explained the method for painting the images:

"One should paint the Vajra Wrathful Deity according to the ritual of the Vajramaṇḍala, as well as the great bodhisattvas, the various devas, and the hosts of mātṛs; this is the supreme method for achieving success through painted images."
Thereafter, one should perform offerings before the image according to the ritual rules, arrange a seat, sit down, bind the root mudrā, and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
By reciting in this manner, all mundane and supramundane dharmas will be fully accomplished.

Furthermore, even if one has not yet attained mastery in the dharmas, but merely constantly upholds and recites them, such a person is able to perform various rites such as veneration and love, summoning, entry and awakening, binding, and release.
Furthermore, he spoke of the various methods for accomplishment:
"If one wishes to destroy all evil beings, one should rely on the rite of Vajrakrodharāja.
If one wishes to shatter all false mudrās, one should manifest a wrathful gaze while reciting the mantra."
"If one wishes to destroy all māras, one should hold a vajra, manifest the form of great wrath, and perform recitation.
If one wishes to perform a rite of restraint, one should manifest the form of wrath and perform recitation, while further striking that direction with a vajra."
"If one wishes to effect various acts of dispersal, one should rely on the rite of the subtle Vajramaitreya.
If one wishes to summon malevolent planets and lunar mansions, one should manifest the wrathful subduing form and rotate the vajra."
"If one wishes to cause others to feel hatred and anger, one should perform the homa rite using iron filings.
If one wishes to dispatch the various yakṣas, one should recite according to the ritual of the Honored One of Great Laughter."
"If one wishes to subjugate the nāgas, one should strike the ground with a vajra while reciting the mantra.
If one wishes to subdue the devas, one should recite according to the ritual method of the Vajranīpata deity."
"If one wishes to summon the various devas and to subjugate or destroy [obstacles], one should perform recitation according to the ritual of the Honored One Who Subdues the Three Worlds.

If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of the King of the Northern Quarter, Vaiśravaṇa, one should press one's hand against an image of Vaiśravaṇa and perform recitation while assuming an expression of wrath."
"If one wishes to seek the siddhi of the deity Vṛddhi, one should perform recitation according to the Vajrapuruṣa rite.
If one wishes to achieve the siddhi of a Kāmadeva, one should perform recitation while assuming a wrathful expression before an image of a Kāmadeva."
"If one wishes to achieve the accomplishment of Mahābrahmā, one should employ the mudrā of the Sublime Joy Vajra.
If one wishes to achieve the accomplishment of Nārāyaṇa, one should employ the mudrā of the Vajra Wheel Chain."
"If one wishes to accomplish the Great Lord Maheśvara, one should employ the Vajra-kṣupa-lāṅgala-mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish the various hosts of Mātṛs, one should rely on the Vajra-gaṇa-rākṣasa rite."
"If one wishes to destroy the heterodox altars and mantra-rites of the various non-Buddhists, one should rely on the rite of the Vajra Great Wrathful Pañjaranātha.
If one wishes to shatter all mountains, forests, and even celestial shrines, one should manifest as the Wrathful Vidyārāja and gaze upon them;
if one wishes to restore them to their former state, one should rely on the rite of the Vajra Wrathful Vidyārāja."
"If one wishes to destroy all māras, one should rely on the fist-method of Vajra-krodha-vidyārāja.
If one wishes to instill fear in others, one should manifest a great and terrible aspect through the method of Vajra-krodha-vidyārāja."
"If one wishes to destroy the enemy army, one should rely on the rite of Vajrakrodha Yakṣa.
If one wishes to scatter and disperse the enemy army, one should rely on the rite of Vajrakrodha Rākṣasa."
"If one wishes to destroy the various devas, one should nail the images of the devas;
if one wishes to accomplish the lord of devas, one should likewise rely on this method.
If one wishes to cause the three realms to tremble with fear, one should employ the Vajra-pralāla mudrā."
"If one desires to be victorious within the three realms, one should rely on the rite of Vajrakrodharāja.
If one desires to cause those in the three realms to enter, awaken, be bound, or be rendered submissive through love, one should employ the mudrā of Vajrakrodharāja."

"If one wishes to effect the summoning and the rite of subjugation through love for the three realms, one should rely upon the Dharma of the Great Bliss Vajra Wrathful King (Mahāsukha-vajrakrodharāja).

The Fourth Chapter: The Great Ritual Manual on the Samādhi of Purifying All Afflictions. At that time, the Blessed One Śākyamuni Buddha further expounded the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Wisdom Seal of Avalokiteśvara, which is the equality of all phenomena.
That is to say:
"Because afflictions are pure, all defilements are also pure;
because all defilements are pure, all transgressions are also pure."
Because all phenomena are pure, all sentient beings are also pure;
because omniscience is pure, the perfection of wisdom is also pure.

If a person receives, upholds, reads, recites, remembers, and contemplates this pure Dharma-gate, although that person constantly dwells amidst the phenomena of desire, they will be free from all afflictions; like a pure lotus flower unsullied by any impurity, they shall swiftly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, having heard the Buddha Śākyamuni teach this Dharma-gate of the purity of the true nature of reality, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifested a smile and spoke this Heart-Mantra of the Multicolored Lotus, the Dharma-gate of the Contemplation of All Phenomena as Untainted and Utterly Pure:

“Hrīḥ. As he spoke this Heart-Mantra, all the Tathāgatas appeared, each possessing the form of Avalokiteśvara and holding a lotus flower in their hands; they all took their places according to the ritual of the fundamental maṇḍala of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara entered the samādhi called "The Seal of Sovereignty over Wisdom that Contemplates All Dharmas.
Emerging from this meditative absorption, he proclaimed this ritual for the Maṇḍala for Subduing All Worlds:

"If a person wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment for this Great Maṇḍala, they should draw the inner maṇḍala within the outer maṇḍala, arranging eight seats for the deities at the four cardinal and four intermediate directions, complete according to the prescribed rules."
In the center of that space, paint a red lotus with eight petals; upon the flower, paint the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
In front of the Bodhisattva, paint the deity Mahāpadma, who has the appearance of a celestial Māra, is crimson-red in color, and holds a lotus, a kusuṃbha flower, as well as a bow and arrow.
On the right side, paint Mahāpadma-Krodheśvara, whose physical appearance is like that of Maheśvara.
Behind him, paint Mahāpadma-Kṛṣṇa, whose physical appearance is like that of Nārāyaṇa.
On the left side, paint Mahāpadma, Lord of Sahā, with the appearance and color of Brahmādeva.
In the southeast corner, paint Mahāpadma Lokeśvara, with the appearance and color of Lokeśvara.
In the southwest corner, paint Mahāpadma Varuṇa, with the color and form of the Great Ocean Dragon King.
In the northwest corner, paint Mahāpadma Sūrya, with the color and form of the Great Sun Deity.
In the northeast corner, paint the Great Lotus Wind Deity with the physical characteristics and color of the Wind Deity.
Furthermore, in the four corners of the outer maṇḍala, paint the images of the four deities, namely: Hrīḥ, Śrī, Gi, and Ti.
Thus, all these devas hold a lotus flower in their left hands and their respective emblems in their right hands;
they each place their emblems at the four gates. First is Siddhivigraha, second is Sarvavigraha, and third is Sugatavigraha.
Fourth is Padmavikrāmaṇa. Having thus drawn the maṇḍala, the ācārya should have the disciple don white robes and cover his face with a clean cloth.

Then, holding a beautiful flower and forming the lotus mudrā, he should lead him into the maṇḍala. He should instruct the disciple to cast the flower with a sincere and solemn mind; wherever the flower falls, that is the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Having attained the status of the deity, one should perform the consecration according to the ritual for consecration in the Lotus Family (*padmakula*).
Thereafter, one should admonish the disciple, saying:
"You should view all phenomena as being like a lotus; all defiling afflictions are purified in this very manner."
He then spoke in verse:
"Just as a lotus of exquisite color, Though dwelling in the mud, remains ever pure;
So too is the nature of greed, hatred, and delusion— Untainted and likewise."
All phenomena whatsoever should be observed in this way:
all dharmas are fundamentally pure; one should extinguish all afflictions.
Constantly abiding in all samādhis, one attains the omniscience of a Buddha.
"Having realized such a Dharma as this, one is named Avalokiteśvara.
Having spoken these verses, he further declared:
"From this time forward, your body shall be pure; whatever you seek for accomplishment shall be fulfilled according to your wishes, until you attain Buddhahood."
"In this way, a disciple who wishes to accomplish the Wisdom Maṇḍala shall likewise achieve accomplishment by relying on the methods for painted images.
Furthermore, it is said:
'For one who has not yet mastered the methods for seeking accomplishment, if they wish to cause all people to be joyful, they should empower a lotus eight thousand times.'"
"If one wishes to extinguish and disperse all evils, one should employ the Lotus Seal of the Great Wrathful King.
If one wishes to cause demons and malevolent spirits to become bewildered and confused, one should employ the Great Lotus Vārāha Seal."
"If one wishes to purify all afflictions, one should employ the visualization and mudrā of the Great Lotus.
If one wishes to cause rain to fall, one should draw the form of a nāga; the practitioner shall sit upon that nāga and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*)."
"If one wishes to dispel darkness, one should employ the Great Lotus Sunlight Seal (Mahāpadmasūryamudrā).
If one wishes to raise a wind or cause it to cease, one should employ the Lotus Marut Seal (Padmamārutamudrā)."

5. The Fifth Chapter: The Ritual Manual of the Great Samādhi of the Empowerment of All Jewels. At that time, the Blessed One Śākyamuni Buddha further proclaimed the teaching of the *Prajñāpāramitā* known as the "Wisdom-Treasury Born of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas":
"If one bestows empowerment, one shall attain the rank of Dharma King over the three realms;
if one bestows precious wealth, one shall fulfill all aspirations."
"If one bestows the sublime Dharma, one attains the equality of all dharmas;
if one bestows food and drink, one attains the happiness of body, speech, and mind.

At that time, having heard the Buddha preach this Dharma-gate of True Principle, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha manifested a great smile and formed the Jewel-Vajra Consecration Garland Seal upon the crown of his own head.
Having bound this mudrā, he spoke this heart-mantra of the Jewel of All Empowerment Samādhis, saying:
"TĀṂ. When he spoke this heart-mantra, the signs and characteristics of all the meanings and phrases of empowerment appeared.
Having thus emerged, they appear in the form of bodhisattvas, each in their respective original positions, according to the ritual of the Jewel Family Maṇḍala.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha enters the samādhi of the All-Consecrating Jewel-Vajra.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he taught the Great Maṇḍala of the Great Maṇi Jewel that Fulfills All Vows:

"If a person accomplishes this maṇḍala, they should draw the inner maṇḍala according to the ritual for the outer maṇḍala. In its center, one should draw an eight-cornered jewel pillar, resembling the appearance of eight maṇḍalas, adorned with jewel garlands, surrounded by a perimeter of jewel-vajras, and provided with various ornaments such as banners, flags, and parasols."

Thereafter, within the maṇḍala, one should paint the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, riding in a carriage drawn by horses, manifesting a great smile, with a body of deep red color, and his two hands forming the consecration mudrā (*abhiṣeka-mudrā*).
In front of the Bodhisattva, one should place all the Tathāgatas and the Bodhisattva Ratnābhiṣeka, who wears a jeweled crown;
on the right side, one should place the Bodhisattva Sarvaratnagarbhadhara;
and behind him, one should further place the Bodhisattva Dharmaratnagarbhadhara.
On the left side, place the Bodhisattva Holding Various Drinks and Foods;
at its four corners, place the Bodhisattvas of Offering, along with precious parasols, banners, pennants, and various kinds of exquisite music.
At the four gates and four corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should duly place the argha vases, the insignia for empowerment, offerings, and so forth.

Having thus drawn the maṇḍala, the ācārya should bind the jewel mudrā (ratnamudrā) and, according to the ritual, lead the disciples into the maṇḍala; by means of the jewel empowerment rite (ratnābhiṣeka), he shall confer the empowerment, as well as the mudrās, signs, and insignia.
From this point forward, whatever accomplishments one seeks shall all be attained in their full perfection.
The ritual procedure for leading disciples into the maṇḍala as described above should likewise apply to the methods for accomplishing feats within the Ratnavajra family.
"If one has not yet mastered the dharmas but wishes to receive the various empowerments, one should bestow the seal of the Jewel-Vajra Empowerment.
If one desires to fulfill all wishes, one should perform recitation at sunrise."
"If one wishes to understand the meaning of all phenomena, one should contemplate all phenomena as pure and like space while reciting [the mantra].
If one wishes to seek various superior flavors, one should visualize one's own body as being like space and recite it a thousand times daily."
"If one wishes to fulfill great vows, one should hold a precious parasol and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
If one seeks the most supreme [attainment], one should employ the precious banner and the vajra mudrā."
"If one desires to seek great renown, one should daily recite [this]. Chapter Six:

The Great Ritual Manual for the Samādhi of the Fist-Mudrā of All Tathāgatas. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha—having attained the wisdom-mudrās of all Buddhas, having maintained the wisdom-fists of all Buddhas, and being the ultimate realization of all Buddhas—further spoke the teaching on the Vajra-prajñāpāramitā of the mental visualization of the Wisdom-mudrā of All Tathāgatas.
That is to say:
because one encompasses the body-mudrā of all Tathāgatas, one is the body of all Tathāgatas;
because one encompasses the speech-mudrā of all Tathāgatas, one attains mastery over all dharmas.
Because one embraces the heart-seals (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one immediately attains all *samādhis*;
because one embraces the vajra-seals (*vajra-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one immediately attains the supreme accomplishment of the three vajra-actions.

"If any person hears, receives, upholds, recollects, contemplates, and explains this Dharma-gate to others, that person shall achieve all dharmas, penetrate all-knowledge, fulfill all undertakings, and even attain the supreme accomplishment of the three vajra-activities, swiftly realizing Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

At that time, when the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi had heard the Buddha’s teaching on this true dharma of the Great Samādhi Vajra Seal of Gathering, he immediately manifested a sign of joy and spoke the heart-vidyā for the accomplishment of the samādhi of all firm vajra seals, saying:

“Aḥ. When this heart-vidyā was spoken, all the Tathāgatas and the entire assembly were transformed into Vajrasattvas; they all bound the Vajrasattva seal and were marked with the supreme accomplishment seal of all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas. Relying upon the vajra three-karma and the great seal-samādhi of the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi, they dwelt within this maṇḍala.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi entered the samādhi of the Wisdom-Seal of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from that concentration, he spoke this Great Maṇḍala Dharma of the Vajra-Samaya of All Seals:
"If a person constructs this maṇḍala, they should draw the outer maṇḍala according to the ritual procedures of the previous maṇḍala, and within its center, draw an eight-spoked wheel."
Within that wheel, eight positions are arranged in sequence; in the central position is established the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi, manifesting a joyful expression and forming the samādhi-muṣṭi mudrā.
In front of this Bodhisattva, place the Supreme Vajra-body Bodhisattva, holding a vajra;
to the right of the Vajra-fist Bodhisattva, place the Vajra-tongue Bodhisattva;
behind the Vajra-fist Bodhisattva, place the Vajra-concentration Bodhisattva, holding a vajra.
To the left of the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi, place the Bodhisattva Paramavajra, holding a vajra.
Furthermore, in the southeast corner of the maṇḍala, place the Bodhisattva Mudrāmuṣṭi;
in the southwest corner, place the Bodhisattva Arthamuṣṭi.
In the northwest corner, one should place the Bodhisattva Jñānamuṣṭi;
in the northeast corner, one should place the Bodhisattva Karmamuṣṭi.
These bodhisattvas all bind their respective fundamental mudrās and hold their own insignia.
Furthermore, one should install the four Bodhisattvas, such as Vajragandhā and others, at the four gates.

Once the maṇḍala has been drawn in this manner, even if there is someone who has not yet mastered this rite, upon entering it, they shall become an ācārya endowed with the accomplishment of all mudrās.
From this point forward, one will certainly attain the accomplishment of all dharmas and swiftly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

If the *ācārya* is to transmit [the teachings] to a disciple, he should immediately form the *vajra-muṣṭi-mudrā*, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala, and bestow the empowerment according to the *vajra-abhiṣeka* rite. Having bestowed the empowerment, he shall recite this verse for them:
"The vajra body, speech, and mind Should be contemplated as being like reflections."
"All mudrās are likewise; this is called the samaya-vow.
As described above regarding the ritual for the disciple’s entry into the maṇḍala, all the mudrā-forms of this family and the methods for accomplishing the maṇḍala are also like this.
Furthermore, for those who have not yet attained mastery, he taught the method of accomplishment:
"If one wishes to accomplish the various mudrās, one should form the vajra-fist at the heart and perform the recitation."
"Furthermore, if one wishes to accomplish all mudrās, one should bind the Great Vajra Fist Mudrā.
If one wishes to gain the love and respect of all sentient beings, one should bind the Vajra Great Bliss Fist Mudrā."
"If one wishes to subdue all sentient beings, one should bind the Vajra Great Fist Mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish all samādhis, one should bind the Vajratāki Mudrā."
"If one wishes to bind and restrain all evils, one should form the Vajrabandha mudrā.
If one wishes to bind and restrain all beings, one should form the Vajrapāśa mudrā."
"If you wish to cause *jaṃbhanā*, you should form the *vajra-lepa-muṣṭi-mudrā*.
If you wish to cause *bhīṣaṇā*, you should form the *vajra-bandha-muṣṭi-mudrā*."
"If one wishes to destroy all evils, one should form the Vajra-Ānkuśī Fist Seal.
If one wishes to perform *vaśya* (subjugation), one should form the Vajrayakṣa Fist Seal."
"If one wishes to destroy all māras, one should form the vajra-kṣepaṇa fist-mudrā.
If one wishes to open and clear all things, one should employ the vajra-śṛṅkhala fist-mudrā."
"If one wishes to cause all to awaken, one should form the Vajrāveśa Fist Mudrā.
If one wishes to perform the *cillita* [subjugation] rite, one should form the Vajracillita Fist Mudrā."
"If one wishes to cause all speech to be [manifested], one should form the Vajra Speech Fist Mudrā.
If one wishes to subdue and restrain all, one should form the Vajra Samādhi Fist Mudrā."
"If one wishes to cause the enemy army to be *mūrcchita* (fainted/stunned), one should form the Great Vajra Speech Fist Seal (*vajravāgmuṣṭimudrā*).
If one wishes to release all evil seals, one should form the Vajra Liberation Fist Seal (*vajramokṣamuṣṭimudrā*)."
"If one wishes to release the various *ḍākinī* mudrās, one should form the Vajra Fist Mudrā for Subjugating the Three Worlds.
If one wishes to destroy the various evil mudrās, one should likewise form the Vajra Fist Mudrā for Subjugating the Three Worlds."
"If one wishes to restrain all mudrās, one should form the Vajrasandhi Fist Mudrā.
If one wishes to cause all mudrās to be as firm as vajra, one should form the Vajramuṣṭi Mudrā."
"If one wishes to seal all things, one should form the Vajramudrī Fist Seal.
If one wishes to destroy all māras, one should form the Sublime Vajra Fist Seal."
"If one wishes to destroy all evils, one should bind the Great Evil Wrathful Vajra Fist Seal.
If one wishes to enter, walk, or stay within water, one should bind the Vajra Prohibitory Fist Seal."
"If one wishes to manifest various forms and images, one should bind the Vajra Fist Mudrā of the Universal Karma.
If one wishes to seek the method for invisibility, one should bind the Invisible Vajra Fist Mudrā."
"If one wishes to accomplish all activities performed while walking or staying, one should bind the Ākāśavajramuṣṭi-mudrā.
"If one wishes to soar through the air with mastery, one should bind the Vajrabandhamuṣṭi-mudrā."
"If one wishes to accomplish the vidyādhara state, one should form the vajra-sword fist mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish the offerings to all Tathāgatas, one should form the vajra-karma fist mudrā."
"If one wishes to master all-knowledge, one should form the Vajrajñānamuṣṭi mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish all aims, one should form the Vajrārthamuṣṭi mudrā."
"If one wishes to accomplish the mastery of all mudrās, one should form the vajra-fist mudrā.
If one wishes to accomplish all activities, one should form the various vajra-fist mudrās."
"If one wishes to accomplish all maṇḍalas, one should form the Vajrapāṇi Fist Mudrā.
If one wishes to cause [the deity] to speak of the three periods of time, one should form the Vajrajihvā Fist Mudrā."
"If one wishes to achieve mastery over Vajrapāṇi, one should form the Vajra-utkṣepa mudrā.
If one seeks to achieve mastery over the Buddhas, one should form the Buddha-vajramuṣṭi mudrā."

Chapter Seven: The Great Ritual Manual of the Vajra-Syllable Wheel Samādhi. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha further expounded the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Transformed Syllable Wheel, which is the absence of intrinsic nature in all phenomena.
That is to say:
"Because all phenomena are empty and lack intrinsic nature, all phenomena are signless;
because they are signless, all phenomena arise."
Because all phenomena are wishless, all phenomena arise from wishlessness.
Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, having heard the Buddha speak this Dharma-gate of ultimate truth, immediately manifested a smile and, representing all Buddhas with the sword of wisdom, spoke this *hṛdaya-mantra* of the supreme Prajñāpāramitā, saying:
“A. When he spoke this *hṛdaya-mantra*, all Tathāgatas gathered like clouds and remained stationed according to the ritual of the previous maṇḍala.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī entered the samādhi called "The Sword of the Self-Naturelessness of All Dharmas.
Emerging from that concentration, he taught the rite of the Maṇḍala of the Samādhi of the Revolving Wheel of Syllables:

"If one is to construct this maṇḍala, one should, within the outer maṇḍala, draw an eight-spoked wheel according to the ritual rules. Within the perimeter of this wheel, one should inscribe the heart-mantras in their proper sequence."

Subsequently, eight positions are arranged in the four cardinal and four intermediate directions; in the central position is installed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, appearing in the form of a youth, with a body as pure and translucent as space, possessing four arms that symbolize the sword of wisdom, radiating light everywhere.

Outside the bodhisattvas, one should place the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas; in the four corners, according to the ritual rules, one should place the four Prajñāpāramitā Sūtras; and at the four gates, one should place the four insignia, namely: a sword, a śakti, a jewel, and a scripture.

Thereafter, the ācārya forms the sword mudrā (*khaḍgamudrā*) or the scripture mudrā (*sūtramudrā*), and according to the ritual, leads the disciple into the maṇḍala. He bestows the wisdom sword (*jñānakhaḍga*) and performs the consecration (*abhiṣeka*). Having performed the consecration, he recites the verse of the dharma-vow for him, saying:
"You shall receive the wisdom sword, Which is equal to the truth of Prajñāpāramitā.
Contemplate the Buddha as being like space; What is thus indicated shall be swiftly accomplished."
"Protecting the Buddha-dharma, I shall extensively deliver all sentient beings;
with this sword, I shall sever karmic obstructions, causing them to be forever exhausted without remainder.
Having spoken these verses, he further addressed them, saying:
“By means of this sublime Dharma, may you accomplish the Prajñāpāramitā and swiftly realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“If one wishes to accomplish the Dharma-maṇḍala, it should also follow the ritual procedure as previously described.”
Furthermore, he spoke of the method for accomplishment:
"If one wishes to realize the samādhi of emptiness, one should contemplate all phenomena as being like space.
If one wishes to realize the samādhi of signlessness, one should contemplate all phenomena as being devoid of signs."
"If one wishes to realize the samādhi of wishlessness, one should contemplate that all phenomena are wishless.
If one wishes to realize the dharma of naturally pure wisdom, one should contemplate the principle of the Prajñāpāramitā."
"If one wishes to sever all afflictions, one should contemplate the True Dharma.
If one wishes to attain the true knowledge of all syllables, one should contemplate the naturelessness of phenomena."
"If one wishes to contemplate the Dharma-body without attachment to words in all places, one should do so by relying on the intrinsic nature of the syllable *ma* and contemplating it as emptiness."
“If one wishes to realize the bodhi of all Buddhas, one should form the vajra-sword mudrā.

Chapter Eight: The Great Ritual Manual of the Samādhi of the Vajracakra of All Maṇḍalas. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha further proclaimed the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā for gathering the wheels of all Tathāgatas into the Great Wheel.
That is to say:
"Because of entering into the equality of the vajra, one enters the wheel of all Tathāgatas;
because of entering into the equality of meaning, one enters the wheel of the great Bodhisattvas."
"Because one enters into the equality of all phenomena, this is the entry into the wondrous Wheel of Dharma;
because one enters into the equality of all things, this is the entry into all wheels.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Citta-saṃbhava-cakra-pravartana, having heard the Buddha’s exposition of this Dharma-gate of True Principle, manifested a smile and spoke the heart-mantra for entering the Samādhi of All Vajras by turning the Vajra-wheel, saying:
When this heart-mantra "HŪṂ" was uttered, all the Tathāgatas and all sentient beings of the three realms gathered together within the maṇḍala like clouds.
Furthermore, from the mind of the Bodhisattva, all maṇḍala-samādhis are produced.
At that time, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas abide according to the Dharma.
Then, the Bodhisattva Dharmacakra-pravartaka, born of a single-minded resolve, enters the samādhi of the seal of all wheels.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he taught this method for entering the Great Maṇḍala of the Wheel of All Samādhis:

"One who constructs this maṇḍala should draw a vajra-wheel within the outer maṇḍala; within that wheel, one should draw the Bodhisattva Dharmacakrapravartana. All the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and the assembly of Bodhisattvas such as Vajrapāṇi should also be drawn according to the ritual procedure of the aforementioned maṇḍala."
In the four corners of that maṇḍala, one should paint the four great bodhisattvas of the Vajra family, namely:
the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva, the Bodhisattva Vajracanda-vighnāntaka, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
At the four gates, one should paint the four insignia.

Having thus painted the maṇḍala, the ācārya then forms the vajracakra mudrā according to the rite and leads the disciple into the maṇḍala. He bestows upon him the vajracakra and confers the empowerment, transmitting the four types of maṇḍalas as well as all the samayas and other dharmas belonging to that family.
"Since the ritual procedures for the disciples are thus, the accomplishment of the deeds within the Vajracakra Maṇḍala should also be performed in this manner.
He further explained the method of accomplishment:
"Those who wish to enter any maṇḍala should form the Vajracakra mudrā and place it at the mouth."
"If one wishes to enter the Great Maṇḍala, one should bind the Great Wheel Mudrā.
If one wishes to enter the various Seal Maṇḍalas, one should bind the Vajra Seal of all Tathāgatas."
"If one wishes to enter the Samaya Maṇḍala, one should form the Great Samaya Wheel Mudrā.
If one wishes to enter the Karma Maṇḍala, one should form the various Vajra Wheel Mudrās."

Furthermore, for the rites of magnetizing, subjugation, sealing, destruction, entering all places, making offerings, and taming all evil beings, one should form the mudrās of the eight great bodhisattvas, or alternatively, form the wheel mudrā.
Chapter Nine: The Great Ritual Manual of the Samādhi of All Vajras. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha further expounded the teaching on the supreme offering of the Prajñāpāramitā.
That is to say:
"Because of generating the bodhicitta, this is the vast offering to all Tathāgatas;
because of rescuing and delivering the realms of all sentient beings, this is the vast offering to all Tathāgatas."
Because it encompasses all phenomena, this is itself the vast offering to all Tathāgatas.
If a person writes down, upholds, reads, recites, memorizes, and contemplates the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, this is itself the vast offering to all Tathāgatas.

At that time, when the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja had heard the Buddha teach this Dharma-gate of reality, he immediately manifested a smile and spoke this heart-mantra of the Sarvakarmāparājita-samādhi, saying:

"Oṃ. As he spoke this heart-mantra, all manner of offerings filled the entire realm of space; furthermore, from within the sky, emanations in the form of bodhisattvas appeared and returned before the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, taking their places according to the maṇḍala.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja entered the samādhi called "Meditation on the Peaceful Arrangement of All Offerings.
Emerging from that concentration, he then spoke this supreme Karma-Vajra-Amogha-Samaya Maṇḍala:

"One who performs this rite should draw an eight-cornered jeweled pillar in the center of the outer maṇḍala. In its center, one should paint the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, his body the color of moonlight, displaying a smiling countenance, and holding ritual implements in his hands."
Furthermore, one should paint the various bodhisattvas according to the ritual rules, namely:
the eight great bodhisattvas, such as Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, each possessing their respective original characteristics and fully endowed with their seals and dharmas.
Furthermore, one should paint four offering bodhisattvas in the four corners, and at the four gates, paint the four insignia (*cihna*) along with various precious implements.

Having painted thus, the ācārya should bind the Karma-vajra mudrā and, according to the ritual, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala; then, by means of the empowerment rite of the Karma-vajras, he should confer the empowerment.
Having conferred the empowerment, one performs four kinds of offerings:
first, prostration through the activity of body;
second, praise of the true and wondrous principle through the activity of speech; [and so forth].
Third, through the mental action of visualization, one contemplates that everything within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) becomes an offering;
fourth, one forms the vajra mudrā with the hands.
This is called the ritual procedure for the disciple’s entry into the karma-maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is taught:
"If one wishes to make an offering with the bodhicitta, one should visualize the mind-vajra.
If one wishes to make an offering with samādhi, one should visualize the purity of all phenomena."
"If one wishes to perform the offering of consecration, one should visualize the various Karma-vajras.
If one wishes to perform the offering of mudrās, one should visualize the various Vajras."
"If one wishes to make an offering with space, one should do so by means of the visualization of the letter A.
If one wishes to make an offering to all maṇḍalas, one should do so by means of the visualization of the various vajra-wheels."
"If one wishes to make offerings with all available requisites, one should do so by means of the visualization of the various vajras.
If one wishes to subdue malevolent beings as an act of offering, one should manifest a wrathful form, perform empowerment, and cast flowers upon them."

Chapter Ten: The Great Ritual Manual of the Vajra Wrath Samādhi. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, the Tamer of the Untamable, performed the Great Wisdom Fist Seal and further proclaimed the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Treasury for Taming All Sentient Beings.
That is to say:
"Because all sentient beings are equal, wrath is equal;
because all sentient beings are to be subdued, wrath is to be subdued."
Because all sentient beings abide in the Dharma, wrath itself abides in the Dharma;
because the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings is firm and stable, the intrinsic nature of wrath is firm and stable.
"Why is this? Because all such subduing is itself bodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrayakṣa, Subduer of All Māras, having heard the Buddha preach this Dharma-gate of subduing, immediately manifested a smile.
Again, manifesting the form of Vajrabhairava and binding the seal of the vajra sharp fangs, he then spoke the heart-mantra of the Great Joyful Mind of Vajra Wrath, saying:
“HAḤ. When this heart-mantra was spoken, all evils were completely subdued, and all sentient beings emerged from the Bodhisattva’s heart and remained according to the rite of the maṇḍala.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrayakṣa entered the samādhi called "The All-Pervasive Expedient Means for Subduing the Wrathful Vajra.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed this ritual method for the Maṇḍala of Vajrayakṣa, the Peaceful Contemplation for Subduing All Evil:

"One who seeks to accomplish this rite should first construct a maṇḍala according to the previously described outer maṇḍala ritual; within its center, one should draw a four-sided maṇḍala using five colors."
At the four gates and four corners, draw eight precious pillars with blazing, radiant flames.

In the center of the maṇḍala, according to the ritual rules, draw the Bodhisattva Vajrayakṣa, his body a deep blue color, appearing most terrifying yet with a great laughing expression, sharp fangs protruding outward, and radiating brilliant light.
Around the Bodhisattva, one should paint the assembly of Vajrayakṣas, who also manifest extremely fierce appearances, as well as the emblems of the Vajra family.
Furthermore, in the corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should paint the seal of the Vajra fangs, and at each of its four gates, one should paint the Vajra emblems.

Having thus completed the painting, the ācārya shall form the Vajra-Sharp-Tusk Mudrā or the Great-Laughter Mudrā and, according to the rite, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala; he should then bestow upon him the empowerment through the Vajra-Sharp-Tusk Empowerment Ritual.
Having conferred the empowerment, the ācārya then assumes the posture of Vajrayakṣa and strikes with the vajra; immediately, the painted image of Vajrayakṣa lets out a great laugh.
When this auspicious sign is seen, the ācārya will know with certainty that he shall attain the state of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of the Field of Medicine.

The ācārya should then perform the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana*), forming mudrās and reciting mantras according to the ritual rules, presenting various offerings, and reading and reciting the teachings of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Having thus performed the offerings according to the ritual, one should emerge from the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, he spoke of the method for accomplishment:
"The method for accomplishment to be performed should likewise follow the ritual of the Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva maṇḍala."
"If you wish to subdue all evils, you should form the Vajra-Sharp-Fang Mudrā.
If you wish to subdue all sentient beings, you should assume a wrathful posture, manifest a great laugh, and recite the heart-mantra."
"If one wishes to seal all things, one should form the Vajra-fist mudrā.
If one wishes to destroy all evils, one should perform the empowerment by assuming that form; then one will be able to destroy them."
"If one wishes to destroy various heterodox maṇḍalas, one should enter their maṇḍala while holding a vajra in hand.
If one wishes to ruin their offerings, one should manifest a wrathful demeanor and perform the recitation."
“If one wishes to terrify all evil beings, one should gaze upon them with a *peyālava* (staring) look.

The *Sūtra of the King of Great Teachings of the Supreme Root Mahāsukha-vajra-amoghasamādhi*, translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Imperially Appointed Grand Officer, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, the Subject Fa-xian, by Imperial Decree. Volume Two. Section Eleven: The Great Ritual Manual of the Samādhi of All Bliss. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha further proclaimed the teaching of the supreme Prajñāpāramitā of all dharmas.
That is to say:
"Because all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are equal, this is the equality of the practice of Prajñāpāramitā;
because all meanings (*artha*) are equal, this is the equality of the meaning of Prajñāpāramitā."
Because all phenomena are equal, this is the equality of the dharma of Prajñāpāramitā;
because all undertakings are accomplished, this is the accomplishment of the undertakings of Prajñāpāramitā.

At that time, having heard the Buddha’s exposition of this Dharma-gate of reality, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi immediately entered the samādhi known as "The Mental Abiding in the Non-empty Maṇḍala of All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke this heart-mantra of the Samādhi of All-Non-Emptiness, saying:
“HŪṂ. As he spoke this heart-mantra, all the dharmas of the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgatas issued forth from his heart and dwelt within the Great Maṇḍala of the True Principle of the Great Samaya.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi prostrated with his head at the feet of the World-Honored One and further expounded the ritual procedure for the Great Samaya Maṇḍala:

"If one wishes to accomplish this dharma, one should draw a great maṇḍala, dividing the interior into eight positions and installing therein the various bodhisattvas, such as the Honored One Who Subdues the Three Realms."
Having thus completed the painting, one should thereafter present various offerings according to the ritual rules.
This is called the Samaya Maṇḍala Rite.
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva further proclaimed the ritual procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of the Visualization of the Vajra of All Samayas:
"Once the outer maṇḍala has been drawn, one should draw a vajra-wheel in its center, arranging eight positions and installing the images of the deities according to the ritual rules.

Furthermore, in the four corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should install the bodhisattvas of the Vajra family according to the ritual rules, and at each of the four gates, one should install the insignia of their respective families."
Having thus completed the painting, one should then present various offerings according to the rite of the Great Samādhi.

Section Twelve: The Ritual Manual of the Outer Vajra Family. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha further proclaimed the teaching of the Prajñāpāramitā for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
That is to say:
"Because all sentient beings possess the Tathāgatagarbha, they are Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
because all sentient beings possess the Vajragarbha, they are the consecration of Vajragarbha."
Because it is the treasury of the Dharma for all sentient beings, it is the turning of the wheel of all speech;
because it is the treasury of the activities of all sentient beings, it accomplishes all tasks.
