At that time, when the assembly of the Outer Vajra Family had heard the Buddha teach this Dharma-gate of ultimate truth, they all raised their voices together and recited this Vajra-Mahāmaheśvara Heart-Mantra, saying:
“NṚ! Having recited this heart-mantra, they further set forth the ritual procedure for the maṇḍala:
“One should draw the great maṇḍala according to the original rite.”
Perfectly symmetrical with four sides, four gates, and four corners, one should draw Maheśvara in the center according to the ritual rules.
Outside, on the four sides and four corners, one should draw the eight presiding deities of the assemblies, namely:

Mahākāla in the east, Nandikeśvara in the south, Mahāgaṇapati in the west, Nṛtyeśvara in the north, Rudrakapālin in the southeast, Caṇḍeśvara in the southwest, Khaṭvāṅgapāṇi in the northwest, and Aṭṭahāsa in the northeast.
Furthermore, draw Nandikeśvara at the eastern gate, Munīśvara at the southern gate, Gaṇakeśvara at the western gate, and Mahālaṅgara at the northern gate;
outside of these, draw the various hosts of bhūtas.

Having thus completed the drawing of the maṇḍala, the ācārya shall bathe, don fresh and clean garments, enter the maṇḍala, present various offerings, and while holding a trident, recite the heart-mantra.
Thereafter, according to the ritual, the disciple is led into the maṇḍala and given a trident. For him, the verse on the samaya is recited as follows:
“Holding this emblem, you shall benefit sentient beings;
Attaining mastery over all desires, All that you do shall be accomplished.”
Having spoken these verses, the Ācārya shall immediately bestow upon the disciple the Wisdom Seal (jñānamudrā) and the rites for generating offerings and so forth.

From this point forward, the disciple shall be freed from all fears, attain all accomplishments within his respective family (kula), obtain great wealth and status, and experience all forms of joy, peace, and happiness.

At that time, the assembly of the outer Vajra family, having spoken this Mahiṣāsuramardinī trident maṇḍala, there were further groups of mātṛs who each bowed their heads at the feet of Śākyamuni Buddha and, with one voice, spoke the heart-mantra for summoning all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi-samaya-hṛdaya-mantra*):
"Vyoḥ. Having spoken this heart-mantra, they further explained the maṇḍala rite:

"One should draw a square maṇḍala with four gates and four corners, arranging the various positions according to the ritual rules. In its center, one should paint the lord Mahākāla in a dancing posture."
Outside the image, in the four cardinal directions and the four intermediate corners, one should paint the eight mātṛkās, namely:
in the east, Raudrī, holding a trident;
in the south, Māheśvarī, holding a rosary;
In the west is Vaiṣṇavī, holding a wheel;
in the north is Kāmarī, holding a bell;
in the southeast corner is Gaurī, holding a sword.
In the southwest corner is Mahākarālī, holding a *cullī*;
in the northwest corner is Vākṣaṇī, holding a *paṇava*;
in the northeast corner is Rākṣasī, holding a *khaṭvāṅga*.
Furthermore, in the four corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should draw the four Rudranāginīs, namely:
Śivā in the southeast corner, Vīruṇī in the southwest corner, Caṇḍī in the northwest corner, and Vaḍavāmukhī in the northeast corner.
Furthermore, one should paint four insignia at the four gates:
namely, Padmaprajñāna at the eastern gate, Aṣṭiśaṅkara at the southern gate, Gṛdhraka at the western gate, and Vīraka at the northern gate.

Having thus completed the drawing of the maṇḍala, the ācārya shall bathe until fragrant and pure, don new and clean garments, enter the maṇḍala, and present all the offerings according to the ritual rules.
Then, having formed the Śvānetī mudrā, recite the heart-mantra.
At that time, if one hears the loud sound of the syllable *vyū*, it signifies that all the noble ones and sages have already gathered like clouds.

The ācārya then releases the previous mudrā and again forms the Mahākāla-samaya-mudrā; he then instructs the disciple to hold a beautiful flower and have a clean cloth cover their face, and leads them into the maṇḍala.
The Ācārya approaches the disciple and loudly utters the sound of the syllable *vī*.
At that moment, the disciple immediately becomes awakened; he then scatters flowers, and the place where a flower falls is the location of the tutelary deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
Having attained the status of the deity, remove the cloth covering the face and cause them to gaze upon the maṇḍala in its entirety, immediately offering incense and flowers as an act of worship.
The Ācārya shall then transmit to [the disciple] the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra), mudrās, insignia (cihna), and other rites of the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Furthermore, he shall explain the samaya-vow, saying:
"One must carefully examine all sentient beings; Do not recklessly transmit the heart-mantra."
"Those who are diligent shall achieve success; those who destroy the Dharma shall be extinguished.
Those who oppose this samādhi will be shattered and ruined in an instant.
Having spoken these verses, he then made offerings according to the ritual with food, drink, music, and so forth.
"When these ritual matters are thus concluded, one should exit the maṇḍala.

At that time, after the assembly of *mātṛkās* had spoken this Maṇḍala of All Accomplishing Seals, there was further the assembly of *mudgaras*, who immediately prostrated with their heads at the feet of the World-Honored One before the Buddha and, with one voice, spoke their own heart-mantras, saying:
"Svā. Having spoken this heart-mantra, they further spoke the maṇḍala rite:
"One should draw the outer maṇḍala with four gates on its four sides, and within it, draw another maṇḍala in the shape of a crescent moon.

If there are people who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, and keep in mind this Dharma-gate, then whatever practices and vows of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas they have cultivated that were not yet fulfilled shall become fulfilled; all their karmic obstructions and burdens shall be extinguished without remainder, and they shall immediately realize the Tathāgata’s Right and Equal Enlightenment.

therefore, he is named Vajrapāṇi, acting as your refuge.
You take refuge in the Buddhas, as well as the Dharma and the Noble Ones."
Then they shall return to me and rely upon my samādhi.
At that time, the lords of the devas and their respective hosts of deities,
having heard these words, addressed Vajrapāṇi in white [verses]:
"Relying upon the holy words of the Bodhisattva, may you deign to show compassion. At that time,
Vajrapāṇi again manifested a frowning expression,
assuming a state of great wrathful majesty, and with an exalted and formidable power, [he spoke].
With a great voice, he subdues the three realms and utters this most supreme vidyā:
while this heart-vidyā is being spoken, all the lords of the three realms—
When the assembly of devas had all subdued their minds and dwelt in samādhi,
they were conferred the empowerment of their respective families.
Having received the empowerment rite, they entreated Vajrapāṇi.
The ritual procedure for the Heart-Mantra is taught;
this is the dharma of the great maṇḍala. Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva shall now explain it:
"Within the outer maṇḍala, one should draw a vajra-wheel in the interior."
Possessing blazing and radiant light, with the subduer of the three realms seated within;
his body is a deep blue color, manifesting expressions of both joy and wrath;
baring sharp adamantine fangs, he sits in the full lotus posture.
He playfully hurls the vajra, its blazing radiance shining everywhere.
Furthermore, in the four directions, he establishes the Vajra Sages;
each holds a symbolic emblem in hand, namely the great vajra.
The trident and the treasure-vase, variously colored lotuses and the like,
are placed in the four corners; as well as the arrow and the khaṭvāṅga,
the wheel, and banners of many colors.
The noble deities of the Vajra Family, according to this ritual of the Great Wheel, are each installed in their respective positions.
First, the seven types of noble ones are installed:
the second is named Vajraprabhā, and the third is named Vajrarāja.
Together with his other retinues: fourth, the vidyādharas who perform song and dance;
fifth, the vidyārājas who guard the gates; sixth, Vajranarta;
and seventh, Bhaiṣajyarāja.
According to the ritual, install the various devas; likewise, place the three honored ones, Mānu and the others, in their original positions.
Install the assembly of female devas and the vidyārājas, such as Aṅkuśa and Pāśa.
Each is established in its own position. Once they have been thus arrayed,
the ācārya assumes a wrathful posture and playfully hurls the vajra.
Entering the maṇḍala, one should recite the mantra of the syllable HŪṂ and assume a posture of great loftiness. Thus subduing the wrathful ones,
one gains the joy of the deity, and the wrathful ones achieve accomplishment.
Thereafter, the ācārya, holding various exquisite flowers in his hands and forming the vajrāṅkuśa mudrā,
shall invoke the tutelary deity as well as the Vajra-sages and holy ones.
The mantra for the invocation is as follows:
"Having thus performed the invocation, the Vidyārāja shall descend,
together with the Vajra-sages and holy ones, to bestow all accomplishments."
At that time, within the maṇḍala, various auspicious signs immediately appeared;
either the sound of the syllable *hūṃ* was heard, or there was a sense of awakening.
Then the ācārya formed the mudrā for subduing the three realms.
Lead the disciple into the maṇḍala and bestow upon them the various Great Illuminations (*mahāvidyā*).
The Vajrāṅkuśa-vidyā is as follows:
"HŪṂ HŪṂ VAJRAPRAHARA VIMATHA. The Triśūla-mahāvidyā is as follows:
"HŪṂ VAJRAŚŪLAGHNI PHAṬ. The Vajragarbha-vidyā says: "HŪṂ VAJRAGHOṢIṄ PHAṬ.
The Lotus Great Illumination (Mahāvidyā) says: Furthermore, he spoke the secret mudrā-vidyā, which possesses great majestic power.
The seal of excellence for all sentient beings, through which the methods of accomplishment are performed,
will certainly bring success in all things.
Then he spoke the great mantra:
"These four ḍākinīs are the most supreme heart-seal mantras;
each of them, by means of their own root-mantra, should be installed within the maṇḍala.
Having spoken these great mantras, one then makes the samaya vow."
He instructs the disciples, causing them to listen attentively.
To bring vast benefit to sentient beings, to increase the Buddha-dharma,
to subdue them so they may attain liberation, and to achieve vajra-siddhi.
Having spoken the vow of samādhi, one should cause the disciple to recite the great vidyā-mantra of the syllable HŪṂ and empower the index finger.
By this, all those sentient beings as well as those evil māras—
By the power of this great vidyā, all shall be thoroughly subdued.
Thereafter, one should bestow the empowerment upon the disciple according to the ritual,
transmitting the fourfold methods of the Vidyārāja in their proper sequence.
The mudrās and their applications, the destruction [of obstacles] and the restoration of life—
by means of these mudrās and mantras, one should provide protection.
Having thus subdued [the afflictions], no further evils shall arise.
"From this point onward, all wholesome dharmas will increase,
and one shall see the accomplishment of all dharmas.
He further spoke of the method for accomplishment:
When the practitioner, before the image, playfully hurls the vajra while reciting the vidyā one hundred thousand times, and having completed that number of recitations,
his merit will be like that of Vajrapāṇi, the wrathful great vidyārāja.
Free from the sufferings of old age, illness, and death, having well subdued all evils,
one shall have no further fears within any world.
Desiring to accomplish the Great Illumination, throughout the four modes of deportment,
Reciting this one hundred thousand times,
the methods for accomplishing all deeds will be perfected in this very life; one will attain mastery over all siddhis,
be freed from all suffering and affliction, and become worthy of receiving sublime offerings.
One who can tame those difficult to tame, Who moves and dwells without fear—
If one desires the accomplishment of the seal, One should bind the supreme seal;
Reciting the great mantra as one pleases, The practitioner shall be seen within the world.
One becomes the Great Wrathful King, and all that is undertaken is accomplished.
If one wishes to achieve samādhi, the practitioner should face east,
form the samādhi mudrā, and recite the samādhi mantra.
By performing all dharmas according to one’s will, they shall all swiftly reach fulfillment.
If one desires to seek accomplishment through the supreme *karma* rite,
by reciting the mantra for the sake of benefit and bliss, all activities will be swiftly accomplished.
Furthermore, the method for the supreme accomplishment is proclaimed as follows:

"It dispels all māras, restrains and subdues heterodox teachings, seals all sentient beings, tames all evils, liberates from shackles and fetters, cures various types of malaria, neutralizes all poisons, and disperses the influence of the planets and lunar mansions."
Those who wish to perform these various rites should all rely on the ritual procedure for the Venerable One Who Subdues the Three Realms.

Furthermore, if one wishes to perform any entry or awakening, as well as shaking, sporting, dancing, singing, writing, or spinning, even up to the summoning of the three realms and so forth, one should rely on the mudrā of the Vajra Wrathful King (Vajrakrodharāja).

"If one wishes to summon all beings into the maṇḍala, or to defeat enemy armies by manifesting illusory transformations, to alter the seasons so that flowers and fruits blossom, or to cause crops to flourish; or to neutralize all evil poisons, medicinal toxins, planetary influences (*graha*), and *ḍākinīs*; or to achieve victory in battle, to establish protective boundaries (*sīmābandha*), to liberate from bondage, and even for rites of magnetizing (*vaśīkaraṇa*) and the like—all these are accomplished by means of the Vajra-Krodharāja Vaiśravaṇa mudrā."

"If one wishes to accomplish the subjugation of the devas and the hosts of nāgas, dispatching the yakṣas as servants; to cause all rākṣasas to be struck with great terror; to tame the hosts of ḍākinīs and mātṛkās; to seize the armies of grahas, nakṣatras, and māras; to utterly destroy false maṇḍalas and incantations; to cause all the valiant ones to be filled with fear; and to accomplish the propitiation of the Four Great Kings, Śakra, Mahābrahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and others; as well as the accomplishment of the bodhisattvas and the Buddhas’ acts of affection; and to summon sentient beings and cause them to abide in samādhi—all such various methods rely upon the supreme *sādhana* of the Vajrakrodharāja."
Then he spoke in verse:
“If one wishes to accomplish this supreme dharma,
one should recite the heart-mantra while manifesting the form of the wrathful deity.”
At that time, Avalokiteśvara further expounded the samādhi of the most supreme and pure dharma:
"To subdue all evils, he manifests as the Lotus Family."
Through the power of the skillful means of all Buddhas, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings,
the Wrathful Great Vidyārāja purifies all the three realms of existence.
Because the desires and natures of sentient beings have not yet distanced themselves from various defilements, [he manifests in this form].
The Buddhas, by their unimpeded power, give rise to a heart of great compassion;
yet, as they have not yet been able to deliver [beings], they teach this samādhi.
This is that which all Buddhas of the three periods of time [have taught].
The great king of samādhis, the intrinsic nature of all phenomena,
is named Vajrajñānaprabhāsa.
Contemplated by all Buddhas, it causes all sentient beings—
All have attained great mastery.
Through great wisdom and compassion, they freely deliver sentient beings,
manifesting the appearance of mastery.
With the right hand opening a lotus leaf, one contemplates one’s own nature while abiding in this samādhi.
Since self-nature is free from all defilements, it is pure and unstained.
Without clinging to any afflictions,
even greed and desire are pure; for all classes of sentient beings,
one should act according to what is appropriate for each.
Having attained the sovereign powers of all Buddhas, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and all other bodhisattvas,
relying upon the power of supreme meditative concentration,
have brought forth the great teachings of dhāraṇī.
Then he spoke the mantra for visualization:
"One should contemplate this heart-mantra as being intrinsically pure;
it is all Vajrapāṇis, up to and including Avalokiteśvara."
Visualize this heart-mantra, pure like a mountain of jewels;
next, visualize the lotus of various colors, from which all the worthy sages are born.
Pervading the entirely pure dharma-realm, it becomes the Great Wheel of Subduing.
Once all karmas have been subdued, the three realms are entirely purified.
To benefit all sentient beings, he taught the maṇḍala rites as the great dharma ritual,
establishing the Buddhas and noble sages therein.
Having attained such supreme purity, he accomplished immeasurable dharmas.
At that time, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas entreated Avalokiteśvara to expound the fundamental Lotus Family, the Great Dharma King Vajra.
The Most Victorious Sovereign then spoke of the maṇḍala:
"Within the outer maṇḍala, draw an eight-petaled lotus inside;
in the center of this lotus, place Avalokiteśvara."
Holding a golden lotus in his left hand, he assumes the form of Maheśvara;
his body is adorned with various jewels, and he wears a crown of five Buddhas upon his head.
Surrounding the Bodhisattva, one should paint the eight World-Honored Buddhas.
The Sublime Samādhi and the Great Lotus, Samādhi and Contemplative Insight, and so forth.
Furthermore, outside the eight Buddhas, one should paint the eight holy beings:
Mahābala, Īśvara, Mahābrahmā, and the Kāmadevas.
“Mahāpadma and Hayagrīva, With the hook and the wondrous Dharma-speech.
He then spoke the heart-mantras of the various sages and deities of the Lotus Family:
“Furthermore, at its four gates, Use the hook, the noose, the chain, and the bell.”
The four minds, clear and distinct in sequence, are established according to the ritual procedures of the Great Maṇḍala.
Visualizing that blossoming lotus, one contemplates the mind and pays homage.
"One should place this great vidyā-mantra upon the deity.
Then he spoke the vidyā-mantra:
"Having heard this vidyā-mantra, Avalokiteśvara is delighted."
All the accomplishments sought shall be attained exactly as desired.
Then, forming the hook seal (*ākarṣaṇamudrā*), recite this supreme vidyā:
“Having thus invoked [him], at that very moment Avalokiteśvara...”
Descend upon the maṇḍala, and all that is performed shall be accomplished.
Thereafter, according to the ritual procedures, lead the disciples into the altar,
transmit the secret teachings, and skillfully bestow all attainments.
Because this samādhi-seal mantra is fundamentally perfect,
one swiftly accomplishes Avalokiteśvara.
In whatever place one dwells, even throughout the four modes of deportment, [one shall attain success].
Visualize the Great Lotus Honored One and perform the rite of accomplishment; whatever one desires will be fulfilled in this world,
as well as the most supreme sensual delights.
Far removed from the sufferings of old age and illness,
together with Vajrapāṇi and others, all shall attain complete perfection by relying upon Avalokiteśvara.
If one seeks the accomplishment of seals (*mudrā*), one should bind the seal and enter meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
For those who seek the accomplishment of *samādhi*, they should bind the *samādhi* seal.
For those seeking all *karma*-methods, they should bind the *karma* seal.
Whatever is difficult to accomplish, all depends upon *samādhi*; through reliance on the Dharma, one attains success.

If there are any karmic obstructions, evil dreams, or inauspicious signs, as well as various calamities, grief, sorrow, and affliction; if one is oppressed by the loss of wealth and treasure or by poverty; or if one faces the hardships of strife, provocation, persistent illness, and the perils of the intermediate state—if one wishes to be free from such matters as these, one must rely entirely upon the Great Lotus Reality *Samādhi* Dharma.

Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate wind, bile, phlegm, and catarrh, as well as various fevers, scabies, leprosy, carbuncles, edema, and consumption, and even to cause the extinction and dispersal of the influence of the *nakṣatras*, *grahas*, and *ḍākinīs*, one should rely upon the ritual of the Great Lotus Seal and Mantra.
"If one wishes to make all things firm and stable, one should rely on the Armor-Bound Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Mudrā.

If one wishes to protect oneself, perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and the maṇḍala, create the vajra-enclosure (*vajraparikṣepa*), and so forth, or arrange offerings such as food, drink, clothing, and ornaments, one should in all cases rely on the Great Lotus Mudrā method."

"If you wish to protect all beings, increase their physical strength and lifespan, achieve valor, diligence, auspiciousness, and freedom from illness; if you seek abundant wealth and treasures, great renown, and the love and respect of all; or if you seek to master samādhi and attain great wisdom and so forth—you should rely upon the supreme accomplishment method of the Great Lotus."
At that time, Vajrapāṇi manifested the signs of great syllables,
filling the entirety of space and bestowing the ultimate meaning of empowerment.
He transformed himself into the Ratna family and abided in samādhi.
Through the purity of contemplative observation, one awakens to all phenomena—
the fundamental ultimate truth.
Like seeing celestial bodies reflected in water, one enters the jewel-like samādhi.
Behold that realm of empty space, Like the color of pure lapis lazuli.
The Bodhisattva Vajraratna Arises from the Gaganagañja;
At that time, with steadfastness, He abides according to his original form.
Through the samādhi of visualization, for the sake of accomplishing sentient beings,
and according to the ritual procedures of all Buddhas as well as Vajrapāṇi,
one desires to perform the empowerment rite by means of the jewel-vajra.
Bestowing the empowerment of the noble ones, may all aspirations be fulfilled.
Through the empowerment of all noble ones, recite this empowerment mantra.
Then he spoke the Great Mantra:
When this great vidyā was spoken, the supreme dharma of its own family,
all the sages and holy ones were born from the Jewel Vajra Honored One;
according to the Jewel Vajra dharma, they conferred empowerment upon all the worlds.
Having conferred all the empowerments, they abide within the maṇḍala,
with the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas rejoicing.
The Lord of the Jewel-Vajra Family then proclaimed the supreme ritual procedure:
Within, draw a great lunar disc, its color like the void;
according to the ritual, draw the constellations and planets.
Draw the Honored One Gaganagañja, as pure as the color of lapis lazuli.
Illuminating all with manifold rays of light,
holding a precious jewel in his left hand and resting it at his heart as if performing an invocation, while his right hand makes the mudrā of granting boons—
around this Honored One, one should paint the four attendant deities.
Furthermore, in the four intermediate corners, one should paint four bodhisattvas:
Abhiṣeka, Ratnagarbha, Pūjā, and Śrī;
each should hold their respective insignia.
The mantras for the four attendants are as follows:
"Vajrasattva jaḥ," "Vajraratna hūṃ," "Vajradharma vaṃ," and "Vajrakarma hoḥ. The mantras for the four bodhisattvas are as follows:

"Vajrāviṣkambhī jaḥ (one phrase); Mahāvajranidhane hūṃ (one phrase); Vajramaṇiratna (one phrase); Tvarāgrya-kevali vaṃ (one phrase); Mahāvajramayi hoḥ (one phrase). All such ritual procedures as these are based upon the Great Maṇḍala rite."

Thereupon, the Ācārya takes various precious flowers and enters the maṇḍala; according to the ritual, he presents offerings and pays homage to the Honored One (the deity), reciting the samaya-mantra as follows:
“Oṃ siddhibuddhi siddhibuddhava siddhi svā siddhi mahāvajraratna vajratāṭṭahāṭṭa traṃ. When this great mantra is recited, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja bestows all accomplishments.
Then, the Ācārya, according to the ritual, forms the *maṇi-muṣṭi* (jewel-fist) mudrā with the hook gesture and performs the invocation of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
The invocation mantra is as follows:

“Oṃ bhu ājñāhi jaḥ | Buvabha-praviśa hūṃ | Saghri-hana vaṃ | Vavagagasyan hu traṃ. When reciting this great vidyā-mantra, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja swiftly descends upon the maṇḍala, and all the dharmas sought by the Ācārya will be fully accomplished.
Thereafter, have the disciple hold various exquisite flowers, form the seal as previously described, and lead them into the maṇḍala to transmit the various dharmas of reality.

From this point forward, the disciple shall obtain all forms of wealth and bliss; whatever they undertake shall be accomplished, and even supramundane dharmas such as those of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas shall be swiftly realized.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is taught:
When the practitioner performs the rite of accomplishment, desiring to benefit the world,
by means of this Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*), all things shall be as desired.
Through the power of the seal of the Sovereign Jewel, one is far removed from the sufferings of old age and illness;
like a great mass of jewels in the world that can fulfill every wish,
so too is the seal of samādhi, capable of accomplishing all manner of deeds.
"When one forms the samaya-fist mudrā and presents various sublime offerings,
performing the accomplishment according to the rite, all that is undertaken will be fully perfected.
He further explained the method for accomplishment:
"Among all ritual manuals, that which is most difficult to accomplish can now be accomplished; this shall be explained here.

If one wishes to summon the bhūtas and cause them to enter samādhi, to abide in firm devotion and love, to fulfill whatever aspirations are sought, to purify the evil destinies, and to achieve the supreme dharmas and so forth—all these rely upon the Vajraratna-abhiṣeka-mudrā-vidyā."
"If one wishes to summon [beings] and perform various rites of auspiciousness, or to abide in methods such as firm devotion and love, all these rely upon the Vajraratna-śrī-mudrā-mantra.

If one wishes to summon [beings] and seek various riches and enjoyments, or to abide in various methods of accomplishment such as firm stability, all these rely upon the Vajraratna-bhoga-mudrā-mantra."

"If one wishes to perform summoning rites (*ākarṣaṇa*) and various offerings, or to abide in practices such as those for steadfastness and even for winning affection (*vaśīkaraṇa*), all should rely upon the mantra and seal of the Vajraratna Offering."
Then he spoke in verse:
“Out of compassion for all sentient beings, Vajrapāṇi has taught this method of accomplishment; the practitioner should receive and uphold it.”
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the most supreme honor of the three worlds,
desiring to purify the phenomena of desire and the rest, spoke this accomplishment for them.
Having extinguished these three poisons, the world becomes nectar.
Furthermore, in order to gather all the nāgas, he spoke this maṇḍala.
He uttered this heart-mantra, saying:
"One should construct a maṇḍala with four sides and four gates."
Paint the forms of the eight great nāgas; paint two at each door, with the heads of all the nāgas facing the doors and their tails extending to the corners of the maṇḍala.
Within the center of the maṇḍala, paint the Nāga King Ānanda.
The nāga king has eight heads.
Within the outer maṇḍala, draw the eight families of nāga kings.
At that moment, the ācārya assumes the form of a great wrathful deity.
One should visualize oneself as the Great Nāga King;
swiftly entering the maṇḍala, one recites the great vidyā-mantra of summoning to invoke all the nāga kings.
And that great mantra says:
"Once the mantra for summoning and invitation has been recited,
all the nāgas will gather like clouds and enter the maṇḍala."
All the three poisons and various afflictions belonging to the ācārya are immediately and completely extinguished.
Then, for the sake of those nāgas, he spoke the vow of samādhi:
"The greed, hatred, and delusion of the world are your three poisons;
by abiding in samādhi, these three poisons shall be extinguished."
From that time forth, no evil can harm the ācārya;
even if he should ingest various poisonous drugs, they shall become nectar.
Possessing great power and valor, he is like the dragon Hayaśroṇi.
All poisonous phenomena can likewise be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, taught the subjugation of all planetary deities (*graha*);
thus, all malevolent planetary deities and the like [are subdued].
Afflicted by the three poisons, one is unable to benefit sentient beings;
through the harm of grasping and so forth, all sinful karmas arise.
To subdue the malevolent planets, he then spoke this heart-mantra:
"When painting the maṇḍala, one should establish four gates on the four sides;
within the maṇḍala, one should paint the lunar mansions and planets according to the ritual rules.
Having thus arranged them, the ācārya [should proceed]."
Entering that maṇḍala, perform the rite of summoning with the hook.
Having summoned them, present offerings and assume a wrathful expression;
standing in the posture of Vajrapāṇi, recite this heart-mantra.
All malevolent planetary deities are instantly subdued.
Thereafter, the ācārya shall exhaust all suffering;
no evils can invade him, and all virtues will increase.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, who possesses great mastery over the Dharma,
for the benefit of sentient beings, further expounded the maṇḍala;
first, he spoke this vidyā:
When this great mantra was spoken, the supreme Maheśvara,
the most excellent of all, for the sake of subduing through the five secret dharmas,
became the supreme subduer of the world.
I shall now proclaim this supreme maṇḍala of the Great Viśva-dharma, the sovereign among all dharmas:
"Draw the ritual enclosure according to the rules, and within it, draw Vajrapāṇi."
And the assembly of the Vajra family.
At the four sides are four bodhisattvas, each holding their respective insignia:
the one in front is Nārāyaṇa, who holds a vajra-wheel in his hand;
To the right is Niṣprapañca, holding a trident;
to the left is Vajrapadma, holding a golden lotus;
and behind is Gaganagañja, holding a vajra.
Furthermore, in its four corners, one should paint four noble beings,
namely: Vajraśrī, Vajravārāhī, and Vajratārā.
The Vajras of Space and so forth each have their own heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*). The mantras of the various worthy ones and sages state:
"In the outer maṇḍala, install the insignia (*cihna*) according to their respective positions."
The devas and mātṛs, together with the world-protecting deities and others,
each dwell securely according to their respective positions.
The lords of the ten assemblies are established there, each holding musical instruments and implements for song.
All are clarified by their original minds, each abiding securely in its own position.
Once this maṇḍala has been established with all the worthy sages,
the ācārya then enters the ritual arena according to the dharma.
To invite the various sages and holy ones, one should form the hook-summoning mudrā.
Recite the mantra for summoning and inviting:
"While reciting the mantra for summoning and inviting, the five great secret lords..."
The Supreme Vajrapāṇi, together with all other noble deities,
immediately descended into the maṇḍala, causing it to remain firm and stable;
thereupon, these noble deities bestowed the supreme siddhi.
Thereafter, the ācārya, following the ritual procedures as before,
shall construct the maṇḍala and perform all the rites of accomplishment,
fulfilling every matter to the utmost, throughout immeasurable and boundless [realms].
Subduing without equal,
all meanings purified, well-expounded by the Buddhas—
this profound Tathāgata family brings about the attainment of all sublime bliss.
This is the supreme tranquility, in which all Buddhas rejoice.
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva further expounded the profound Dharma—
subtle, inconceivable, vast, and the most supreme illumination.
Pure and originally without marks, Unconditioned and inexhaustible—
this is the true ultimate.
Great bliss and wondrous joy, By means of the truly pure dharma-realm.
Thus benefiting sentient beings,
bestowing all accomplishments, and skillfully granting the Dharma of peace and happiness,
one awakens through the entry of the vajra, thereby awakening all sentient beings.
This is the secret ultimate truth, the definitive vajra-possessor;
it is the foremost ritual manual, the supreme,
invincible Great Samaya of all Buddhas.
Accomplished through the inconceivable, adorned with the kings of all jewels,
resting upon a ground of wondrous tranquility, it is the abode of the Great Muni.
There is great delight and sublime bliss, and the natural sounds of celestial music.
This is the supreme delight;
endowed with manifold offerings, it is the supreme satisfaction.
The incomparable jewel palace is the supreme abode.
To deliver immeasurable sentient beings is the supreme accomplishment.
Thus, as Vajrasattva, one cultivates the conduct of Samantabhadra,
guides sentient beings, and realizes the state of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Regarding the supreme accomplishments:
Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord, possesses mastery over all wondrous sensual pleasures and brings them to complete fulfillment.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme heart-mantra:
When this great vidyā-mantra was spoken, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, born from the five secrets, became the noble being of the true seal (*tattvamudrā*).
He constantly bestows all sensual pleasures; he is the supreme Maheśvara.
The fourfold assembly of noble beings, all transform and benefit sentient beings.
This Dharma is the most supreme of all accomplishments in the world;
because it increases the ultimate truth, one becomes richly endowed with the great wealth of the sages.
Able to bring about great accomplishment, bestowing vast benefit and bliss.
The countless sages and saints are none other than Vajrasattva;
now he shall proclaim the supreme secret vidyā-mantra of all those sages and saints:
"If anyone upholds such a secret vidyā,
that person shall obtain all mudrās and accomplish all dharmas.
Furthermore, this ultimate [teaching] is said to be the supreme method of accomplishment."
By means of such dharmas, whatever is performed shall reach its ultimate consummation.
If there are practitioners who have mistakenly committed various sinful deeds and have not yet achieved success regarding the various secret dharmas, [they shall attain it through this].
If one practices according to this Dharma, all things will be perfectly fulfilled.
For those who wish to achieve accomplishment— whether for a single day,
a month, or even a year— it is sufficient to act according to one's own capacity and strength.
First, one should follow the ritual procedure to paint an image of Vajrapāṇi.
His body is like the color of the moon;
upon a great lotus, he sits in the full-lotus posture, assuming a majestic and exalted stance.
The body is adorned with various ornaments, blazing with manifold radiant colors;
according to the ritual for the Buddha’s consecration, the left hand holds a precious bell and the right grasps a vajra.
Furthermore, paint four noble sages, with two placed on each side, all in a posture of uplifted majesty.
These are known as the Four Close Associates (*catvāraḥ upaniṣadaḥ*): one is the color of a white lotus, while the remaining three are like blue lotuses.
Behind Vajrapāṇi is the Honored One Kīlikīla;
furthermore, on the right side, one should paint the Great Vajra Honored One,
his right hand in the gesture of drawing an arrow and his left hand holding a jeweled banner.
Furthermore, on the left side, one should draw Pārihasa.
These various noble ones (āryas) should be depicted with the appearance of jewel consecration (*ratnābhiṣeka*).
Having painted these images, one may alternatively perform meditative visualization (*bhāvanā*).
Furthermore, those who make offerings, or those who are able to rejoice [in others' merit],
shall attain ultimate liberation, and all their deeds will accord with their wishes.
Such is the secret dharma of the image of Vajrapāṇi.
This is the supreme great bliss;
one shall attain the supreme bliss and accomplish the pure dharma.
By means of this pure dharma, this is the true secret meaning.
Furthermore, he spoke of the maṇḍala:
"One should select a pure location, such as an excellent grove or a monastery vihāra."
Having selected such a place, adorn it with various jewels,
hanging bells and necklaces, banners, streamers, and parasols;
with incense, flowers, and manifold music, decorate it according to the ritual.
Thereafter, one performs the accomplishment of the secret maṇḍala.
Having performed the rite of accomplishment, all the noble deities are perfected.
Those who enter this maṇḍala, the great secret, [attain success].
Becoming a Vajrācārya, all that one desires, wishes for,
and delights in shall swiftly be fulfilled.
Having bathed to become pure, one should anoint the body with exquisite incense.
Wearing a new, clean upper garment and adorning the body with jeweled garlands,
holding various exquisite flowers in hand,
one enters the maṇḍala while reciting the Vajra-gīti-vidyā.
Then he spoke this song of illumination:
"Having entered the maṇḍala, holding various exquisite flowers in one's hands and forming the Buddha-eye mudrā, one should then recite this heart-mantra:"
"Cast flowers and perform prostrations.
Regarding the procedure for prostration, it says:
"Having cast flowers and performed prostrations, one relies upon Vajrasattva."
"Assuming the posture for conferring empowerment, holding the vajra and bell,
recite the Empowerment Samaya.
The mantra for empowerment is as follows:
“The ritual mace symbolizes the principle of ultimate reality; shaking the bell produces the sound of the Dharma.
Samādhi is the Great Seal; abiding therein, recite the heart-mantra.
One who holds this bell and mace becomes Vajrapāṇi.”
This great ācārya is no different from Vajrapāṇi.
This supreme secret, the dharma of the three kinds of samādhi, accomplishes the maṇḍala;
it is most excellent and beyond compare.
Furthermore, he spoke of the method for accomplishment:
"Most profound and ultimate, by virtue of this ultimate dharma, one attains certain accomplishment."
Furthermore, if there are practitioners whose three karmas are not pure and who have not yet attained accomplishment, they shall all attain perfection.
The practitioner should act according to the Dharma, first fashioning an image of a Bodhisattva.
Whether through modeling, painting, or carving, one should present various offerings before an image of a Bodhisattva;
holding a vajra bell and ritual scepter,
by means of the three samādhis and the great vidyās for summoning, [one performs the rite].
Performing the rites according to the ritual manual,
all the great mantras for summoning should be used with the summoning mudrā,
as well as the supreme vidyā-mantra.
And that great illumination says:
"The fundamental great secret, the dharma of the three kinds of samādhi—
therein one should rely upon the tutelary deity to accomplish all offerings."
To make offerings to the Great Illumination, one should perform songs, dances,
and the like. Then, he spoke the ritual for the great offering of the supreme accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, the great secret samaya.
Regarding the Vajra dance, song, and so forth,
the supreme vidyā-mantra says:
"The supreme great secret, the threefold samaya-dharma."
Abiding in all accomplishments, this great dharma ritual manual is like the rite of that deity; the application of mudrās is likewise so.
Reciting the heart-mantra, one speaks of all the Tathāgatas.
Abiding in the accomplishment method, the supreme true meaning,
the great secret samādhi, and the vajra dance and song—
these are the illuminations of all the most eminent dharmas.
And he spoke that vidyā-mantra:
"This is the root mahā-vidyā, the dharma of ultimate reality;
if a person recites it according to the ritual, that person shall become a holy being."
Having attained mastery over the noble wealth, one is able to accomplish all difficult tasks.
This Vajrasattva accomplishes the supreme secret and encompasses all great siddhis.
Swiftly summon Vajrapāṇi; through the dharmas thus accomplished, one shall gather great wealth and joy.
This supreme dharma should be pursued until various colored lights are seen, or other auspicious omens appear.
Once the ācārya has seen [this], he immediately attains great wealth and happiness;
all ritual procedures (*vidhi*) are accomplished, and everything is performed according to his will.
This is called the "Root," the method of the three kinds of samādhi.
When these rites of accomplishment are performed, all the noble sages descend.
According to this dharma of the deity, so it is with all the noble sages;
their songs, dances, and various rituals are likewise identical to those of the original deity.
To awaken the tutelary deity, one should employ the root mantra,
shake the bell, and perform song and dance;
using either the karma-mudrā or the samaya-mudrā— such are the various ritual procedures.
Awakening by means of the vajra-entry, one should cause all to be alert;
accomplishing all samādhis, one transcends the dharmas of the tutelary deity.
This is the supreme secret, the threefold reality-dharma.
Vajra dance, song, and so forth— these constitute the supreme accomplishment.
The practitioner who performs the rite should, according to their inclination and capacity,
select an especially excellent site, such as a palace or a grove.
Whether with jewels or various flowers, one should adorn that supreme site.
The practitioner should bathe and put on fresh, clean, and exquisite garments;
thereafter, they should install the Honored One’s image, whether it be a painted portrait or a sculpted statue.
Having laid out the cloth mandala, perform the Buddhist rites strictly according to the dharma.
Before the image, the practitioner, following the ritual manual of the *iṣṭadevatā*,
holds the vajra bell and *ghaṇṭā* and performs the rite of awakening.
Having summoned each [deity] and established them in their places, perform the offerings to achieve accomplishment.
Once accomplishment has been achieved, throughout the four modes of conduct—
whether in speech or in jest— one may act according to one's will in every situation.
The supreme secret wheel accomplishes all that is desired;
possessing mastery over all siddhis, one is liberated from the sufferings of old age, sickness, and death.
Thus, like Vajrapāṇi, one is the king of the Vajra family.
Master of all seals, whose form is invisible,
Liberated from all fetters and bonds, He gathers in all sentient beings;
Able to act as the great sovereign, He skillfully effects all creation and destruction.
Performing all acts of love and veneration, the most supreme among all accomplishments,
the great sovereign of the world, the highest and foremost bliss—
like a sea of pure lotuses.
This is the erecting of the Dharma-banner, Highly manifest, transcending the three realms;
all shall obtain excellent and supreme benefit.
I shall now explain the fundamental and most supreme Dharma of the three kinds of samādhi.
The ritual for the accomplishment of offerings, as well as the various methods of summoning and so forth—
this secret great bliss is that which all Buddhas rejoice in.
The hand-seal of the Vajra-pāṇi gathers the minds of all sentient beings.
This Vajrasattva extensively cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra;
sovereign like space, arising from the truth of self-nature,
a single dharma gives birth to the boundless, like a sea of pure lotuses.
This most supreme and wondrous bliss, profound and great secret,
is able to bring about all accomplishments; it is the erecting of the banner of the sublime Dharma,
through which one attains such accomplishment as this most supreme and wondrous Dharma-bliss.
The Sūtra of the King of Great Teachings, the Supreme Root of Great Bliss, Vajra-Āmoghā Samādhi, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Five.

Section Twenty-Two: The Ritual Manual for the Great Samaya Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi further expounded the ritual manual for the consecration of disciples according to the Great Samaya Dharma of all Buddhas:

“Any who wish to receive the secret consecration of the Great Samaya of all Buddhas must first give rise to the supreme, secret *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* mind of all Buddhas, which is identical to the self-nature purity of all Buddhas.”
The Ācārya first imparts this supreme secret heart-mantra to the disciple, saying:

"Oṃ sarvayogāyavāk-citta-mudrāyāmī. Having imparted this bodhicitta-mantra, one immediately attains the stage of non-retrogression of all Buddhas, subdues all malevolent spirits and heterodox paths, and becomes a Buddha and a Bodhisattva.
Next, he bestowed this vidyā-mantra, saying:

“*Uttarādhyeṣatāparāṅmukhībhūtacittamanuttara ekam | Vajramanyasapratitiṣṭha piṅga dvitīyam | Hrīdye hrīdye nāthu tṛtīyam | Surate samayasattva ho caturtham | Vajrasimhyatha suḥaṃ pañcamam.*” Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva grants it all to those who seek the method for the supreme accomplishment.

The Ācārya shall transmit the teachings to the disciple according to the Dharma, having the disciple cover their face with a clean cloth and hold various kinds of exquisite flowers. Thereafter, he shall lead the disciple into the maṇḍala. The disciple, with single-minded earnestness, shall make a great vow and scatter the flowers they hold at will; wherever the flower falls, that is one's own tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Once the practitioner has attained the status of the Honored One (iṣṭadevatā), the face-cloth is removed.

At that time, the ācārya, following the consecration rite of the Buddha Family, pours the pure water of the vajra upon the crown of the disciple’s head. Next, he imparts the three kinds of samaya-dharmas, and then bestows the oath of samaya, saying:
“Having received this consecration, You shall abide eternally in samaya.”
Thus all phenomena are accomplished.
You should uphold and accept them with faith, abide in the steadfast samādhi,
and initiate authentic practice.
"The method of the secret initiation is the secret seal (*mudrā*) of all Buddhas;
should one give rise to a mind of contempt, one will immediately fall into hell.
Having spoken these vows, he then bestowed the vajra upon his disciple and recited for him the mantra for holding the vajra:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-mahā-samaya-tattva-dhiti-stoma-viśodhani. (1)
MAHĀVAJRADHARA IDAN SARVABUDDHA TVAṂ VAJRA VAJRADHARA SVĀHUṬA.
Tvaṃ pihe sadā dharaya mahāvajradhara pratimandi tvaṃ nanta sarvatathāgata.
*Paramamahābodhicitta-mahāsattva-patigraha-nakṣatra-dhāraṇī-maitrī-hṛdaya* (12)
HĪ VAJRA GARBHE PADME ŚRĪ HĪ VAJRANAMASITAṂ SAMAYA SATVAṂ PŪRVĀŚAḤ. Having transmitted this vidyā,
one should bestow a name upon the disciple according to the initiation of their respective tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Having established its name, it proceeds to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), because it does not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Why is this so?
It is solely by virtue of receiving these three kinds of samādhi dharmas that this occurs;
for these samādhi dharmas are in reality non-existent and cannot be apprehended, as they arise from the root and supreme source of the conduct of Mahāsukha-Vajrasattva Samantabhadra.
Having expounded these five supreme and true secret dharmas, he further admonished his disciples, saying:

"This dharma is the most supreme, the lord of the three realms of existence, the foremost of all sovereigns, and the unsurpassed path of reality. It is the pure intrinsic nature of all Tathāgatas; because it realizes that the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings is pure, the intrinsic nature of the three realms of existence is likewise pure, thereby manifesting the principle of reality."

This supreme secret dharma is the vajra bell; it can awaken all the Tathāgatas and all the worthy sages. This dharma-offering can further awaken all phenomena, and by means of this dharma, one awakens all sentient beings and eliminates all karmic obstacles. This is called the Vajra Awakening Dharma; it is capable of accomplishing feats such as subjugation and love, and is the most wondrous expedient for purifying the three realms of existence.

You should develop deep faith and acceptance toward these ritual procedures for this supreme secret samādhi. Within the three realms of existence, this dharma can bring an end to all suffering and cause one to attain sublime bliss; it is a teaching of great skillful means that benefits the world, and its practice, when accepted with faith, is definitively true.

"If a practitioner cultivates this sublime Dharma, even if they are amidst the five desires and experience various pleasant objects, they will be able to practice according to the Dharma without any hindrance."
Why is this? Because this is the incomparable, secret, supreme Mahāyāna dharma of the wondrous samādhi of all Tathāgatas; therefore, one should diligently practice it.

If one does not violate this Samādhi of the Secret Seal of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, that person will certainly abide on the stage of firmness and give rise to the mind of non-retrogression; this is called Vajrasattva attaining the realization of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Then he spoke in verse:
"Bodhisattvas dwell in the world For immeasurable and incalculable eons;
For the sake of all sentient beings, They bring about vast benefit."
Abiding in the samādhi of skillful means, one accomplishes great meritorious karma;
as a Great Sovereign of Vidyā, desiring to benefit sentient beings,
one achieves all things at will through this method of samādhi.
Even those who have committed sinful deeds shall encounter no obstacles and will achieve their desires.
These supreme masters of mastery shall fully accomplish all secret dharmas.
If one practices according to this Dharma, one can benefit both oneself and others;
having correctly sealed all phenomena, one will certainly achieve all accomplishments in their entirety.
By performing the various rites of union, one reaches the end of suffering and attains immeasurable bliss.
Thus, O Vajrapāṇi, whoever can hold this secret vajra in their hand shall obtain all accomplishments.

"Furthermore, the ācārya shall confer the prophecy upon the disciple, according to the ritual for the prophecy of the Vajra-Abhiṣeka of all Buddhas and employing the dharmas of the Great Seals (mahāmudrā) of all Buddhas."
"Once the disciple has received this prediction, they shall immediately transcend all states of existence and enter the realm of all Buddhas.
Then he spoke the mantra of the prediction: "Oṃ īkṣaṃ me karomi taṃ. (1)
vajrasattva satata-gata-bhāvam nirlayato 'tṛptam ātmabhāvasiddhyai.
Oṃ vajranāmadheya tathāgata siddhisamayas tvam praviśa svāhā.
"If a person obtains this great mantra-seal of the prophecy of all Buddhas,

and honors, believes in, and receives it, that person shall immediately cause all the Tathāgatas, the great Bodhisattvas, Vajrapāṇi, and others to descend into the maṇḍala, and they shall bestow upon them the prophecy of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Once this person has received the prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*), all the Tathāgatas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas will regard them with reverence and affection, bestowing upon them all methods of accomplishment (*siddhi*).
The Tathāgatas dwell securely within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), which is as vast and boundless as space.
At that time, all the Buddhas simultaneously offered consolation and praised him, speaking these words:
"This Ācārya has attained the samādhi of all Buddhas and is equal to all Tathāgatas."

If a person attains this supreme secret and is comforted and praised by it, all their karmic offenses shall be dissolved at that very moment; they will be extinguished without remainder, forever freed from suffering and affliction, invisible even to the devas, fearless in all their actions, exhausting the sufferings of the three realms of existence, and accomplishing the supreme Dharma.

Furthermore, this most supreme method of subduing should always be maintained and settled in samādhi; this is what all Buddhas have equally proclaimed. One must not abandon the bodhicitta; through the adamantine secret seal (*vajramudrā*), enlightenment will certainly be attained. These teachings of the Buddhas must never be forsaken, even for a moment.
Even if you should become confused, you may sacrifice even your own body, but you must never for a moment abandon the supreme Dharma of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, do not cast aside or treat with contempt the vajra bell, the vajra scepter, or any of the secret mudrās.

One should revere the ācārya as equal to all Buddhas; if one treats the ācārya with contempt, it is to treat the Buddhas with contempt. Such a person shall undergo manifold sufferings and lack spiritual majesty; they will be afflicted by various fevers, malignant poisons, and *ḍākinīs*, seized by the *nakṣatras* and hosts of māras. Constantly disturbed by such calamities, after the end of their life, they shall fall into hell.

Therefore, you should know that the ācārya is the Great Master; one should always respect, revere, and make offerings to him. As previously stated, none of the various sufferings and afflictions will be able to invade [the practitioner], provided they respectfully honor and make offerings to the ācārya.

Why is this? This Ācārya is truly difficult to encounter even throughout the course of incalculable *koṭi* kalpas; it is through this Ācārya that one awakens to the path of Bodhi and attains the fruit of Buddhahood. Therefore, the disciple should constantly make offerings according to the ritual procedures of the Root Dharma. This is equivalent to making offerings to all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas; by accomplishing the supreme Dharma, one obtains excellent fruits, becoming no different from the various worthies and sages. Having received empowerment, one realizes the station of the Dharma King, acts as the sovereign of the three realms, subdues the armies of Māra, and dwells in the ground of tranquility, certain beyond doubt of the Bodhi of the Buddha-fruit.
After Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva had thus expounded this consecration maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas, he further spoke these words:
"As previously described, this is the supreme secret of all Tathāgatas, which provides consolation and causes one to abide in the samādhi of all Tathāgatas."

The Ācārya and his disciples shall cause the Great Bodhicitta to arise and immediately abide on the stage of non-retrogression; they should contemplate [the Ācārya] as being the most supreme and ultimate Buddha. Why is this?

This refers to the preceptor and the disciple, who are able to give rise to the supreme, great bodhicitta of all Buddhas; because they have given rise to this great mind, they immediately abide on the stage of non-retrogression, never again to fall back.
Because they do not regress, they will certainly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Since they realize awakening in the present, they will certainly and equally realize that *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the future.

Furthermore, because both the ācārya and the disciple are fully endowed with all the practices associated with Vajrasattva, the Tathāgatas provide them with consolation through the most supreme secret.
"Furthermore, as previously stated, those who abide in the samādhi of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas shall realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This so-called fundamental samādhi of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas is the supreme method of accomplishment."
If one abides in this samādhi, one realizes the state of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.

Therefore, if you wish to exhaust all suffering and affliction, you should give rise to a heart of profound respect for the ācārya; you should constantly provide protection, uphold, believe in, praise, revere, and make offerings to them, never flagging or withdrawing for even a moment throughout the remainder of your life.
Furthermore, one should know that this ācārya causes others to give rise to faith and reverence, to serve and make offerings;
he has already perfected the three vajra-karmas and eternally abides in the most supreme and ultimate samādhi of all Buddhas.
"This great secret dharma should not be transmitted to demons, heretics, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the like.
After Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva had spoken these true teachings of all the Buddhas and bodhisattvas, he further spoke in verse:
"One should give rise to great faith and profound respect toward the ācārya."
That Ācārya is the inexhaustible samādhi,
the source of supreme great bliss, equal to all Buddhas without distinction.
By means of the Ācārya, one attains the supreme ultimate.

"Furthermore, Ācārya, you should simply enjoy various riches and pleasures, as well as the finest flavors of diverse foods and drinks, even including such matters as song, dance, and laughter; yet, by reciting according to the rite while employing the root mudrā and performing secret offerings, you shall attain the accomplishment of your goals."
He then spoke the vidyā-mantra for the secret offerings of dance, song, and so forth of Vajrasattva:
“HŪṂ. The vidyā-mantra for the secret offering of all the Tathāgatas: “A.
The vidyā-mantra for the secret offering of the Honored One who Subdues the Three Realms:
The secret offering mantra of the Honored One Padmagarbha is: "Hīḥ.
The secret offering mantra of the Honored One Gaganagañja is: "Traṃ.
With such offerings as these, one accomplishes the method of secret offering by means of these five heart-mantras.
Furthermore, he taught the supreme secret *viśva-mudrā* offerings, as well as the ritual manuals, insignia, and *mudrā* methods for the various holy beings such as Vajrasattva:
"All insignia should be fashioned from gold, silver, auspicious wood, and so forth, each according to its own root method, and installed within the maṇḍala."

At that time, the disciple should perform offerings according to the Viśva-mudrā rite. By virtue of this Viśva ritual, all the disciple’s sufferings, fevers such as malaria, various diseases, poisons, *ḍākinīs*, malevolent spirits, the seizing of evil planets, demonic calamities, and karmic actions leading to the miserable realms are entirely extinguished. Their wholesome karma increases, and they attain the ultimate union with the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Buddhas.
In accordance with this ritual for the offering of the supreme secret Viśvavajra-mudrā of Vajrasattva, all the worthy deities and sages each perform offerings by means of songs of entering samādhi.
"This is called the supreme accomplishment offering for the Viśva-samādhi.
Then he spoke the root Vajrasattva-karmakula Samādhi-vajra-gīti:

"Sarva-anurāga-sukha-manas-santvaṃ | Vajrasattva-sulabha-samayā-bhava me || Mahāsukha-nirdeśa-utsṛja | Pratibhāsa-jñāna-kulapratnata ||" He further spoke the Supreme Secret Samādhi-vajra-gīti of the Sarvatathāgatakula:
"Vajrasattva saṃgraha | Vajraratna mantrita | Vajradharma gāyana | Vajrakarma kuru va. Furthermore, he spoke this supreme secret vajra song for entering the samādhi of all Vajra families:

"HŪṂ Vajrakarī-mukha-śarāya NAMAḤ (1) | ŚRĪ-Vajrarāgasamayāya NAMAḤ (1) | Khaḍgavajra-pūrṇāya NAMAḤ (1) | ŚRĪ-Vajra-kaṇṭhakalāpāya NAMAḤ (1) |" Furthermore, he spoke this supreme secret song of the entry into samādhi for the entire Lotus Family, the Vajra Song:
"Ghaṭi nari rudra lalita nautamugra-jana-suhṛd... (1)
*Prabhaṃkari gajakumbhābhedini krodhadāramūrti-jagadīnāśatāṅkuśe gajakuñjarasamaya-santāpaviprakaraṇe.* (5)
*Komalamanojñavegajidbhinne padma samayaprasanne mamābhimanorājye.* Furthermore,
he spoke the supreme secret vajra song for entering the samādhi of the Sarvavajra Family:
“*Sarva-piśāca-pramardana saṃjñā-cakṣaya-niti prama-sarva-gara hītu vija-yuścarāyatā śrī-vajra-ratna-bhava-mi sukaṇa.*” Then he spoke the *mudgara* song of the Three Honored Ones:
“*Pṛp-vaṣa.*” Then he spoke the song of the Four Holy Ones:
“*Hrīḥ hūṃ śrī-vyu.*” Then he spoke the songs of the various Nāga Kings:
Furthermore, *Pupu* spoke the Vajra Song of the Great Medicine Lord Vajrapāṇi for the offering of the *argha*:

*Sarva-ṛga-maṇḍala-ni-danam | Vajra-dhara-krama | Vimariṇa-vigra vigra | Bañju-tsada-naya-nāśaya | Hana daha paca | Bhasmi-kuru krodha | Hūṃ karomataṛṇa-aṅ.* Furthermore, he spoke the Vajra Song of Entering the Samādhi of the Supreme Secret of the Supreme Sovereign Great Maṇḍala:
*Ghaṭṭa jvala maṇḍalasaroruca-vapu-virājasi | Pralayānala-kuṭīkara-prajvālamahāpavanibbatti ghaṭṭa ghaṭṭa nivartaya nibbatti sukhasantamānanidejana-rūpadharin || 3*
*Sarvārghacāmarīcita-sūrpabṛhat-darapāninā-ghaṭciga-ganamiva sarvasaṃsthitu-jagad-anuyodhadu-viśuddhanaya | Taṃ vajrasattva-sidhyamāye śiṣa-vinaya-vinayadhāsa-sukhe-vīya ||* Furthermore,
he spoke the Vajra Song of the Three Samādhis, the most supreme secret within the most supreme secret ritual:

“Oṃ praviśa vagvan mahāsukhamuṣṭibharaṇa sarvasiddhisukhaparamaṇa mayā paramasukhatmasiddhya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ pra-sidhya svāhā. By means of such supreme, profound, and secret songs of the vajra of the reality of the three samādhis, all sought-after accomplishments shall be fully realized.

This is the Great Viśva-samaya Offering within the supreme secret ritual manuals of all Tathāgatas. By means of this offering, Vajrasattva immediately descends, and one attains the sovereign accomplishment corresponding to Viśva.
Then he spoke in verse:
"This fundamental ritual manual, which skillfully accomplishes all activities,
possesses great secret supernormal powers, and is able to erect the great banner of the Dharma."
One attains the inexhaustible meaning and flavor, accomplishes tasks with certainty,
acquires the complete noble wealth, and perfects the ultimate Dharma.
This great secret of Viśva is that which can bring to fruition even what is difficult to accomplish.
All samādhis, the bliss of dwelling in tranquility and mastery,
and whatever the mind desires, are entirely without obstruction.
Even if worldly people do not cultivate various meritorious deeds, [they still attain these].
Lacking the power of superior virtue, yet because of the obstruction of sinful karma,
one enters this maṇḍala to seek the accomplishment of what is to be done;
according to the root ritual manual, one shall obtain whatever is desired and wished for.
All shall attain full perfection.
Among all dharmas, none can surpass it; even if one should transgress samādhi, commit various sinful deeds, or be afflicted by the influence of the lunar mansions and planets, [it remains supreme].
If one encounters various demonic disturbances, by entering this maṇḍala, all that is undertaken will be accomplished;
by following the ritual, one shall obtain great benefit.
Even if one has not previously entered, one may accomplish the maṇḍala.
"If one performs this mandala rite, it will truly be many times superior.

**Chapter Twenty-Three: The Section on the Ritual Procedures for Universal Correspondence.** At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva further expounded the supreme secret method of accomplishment for the three great samādhis of all Tathāgatas:

"The three great samādhis are what are known as the Buddha-jewel, the Dharma-jewel, and the Saṅgha-jewel. These are the great sublime bliss, the great ultimate, the supreme tranquility, and they abide equally as the source from which all phenomena arise."

If there is a practitioner who, according to the ritual, constructs an image and paints the Three Jewels within it—depicting the Bodhisattva’s form clad in adamantine armor, wielding adamantine weapons, and holding various wondrous jewels—then by means of this painted image, the supreme maṇḍala is accomplished.

Thereafter, one should select an excellent location such as a palace or a vihāra, adorn the ground with incense and flowers arranged in rows, and the practitioner, performing the accomplishment according to the ritual, will immediately attain perfection.
He then spoke the supreme heart-mantra of the three great samādhis of all Tathāgatas:
"Oṃ bhuḥ khaṃ. Having spoken this mantra, he further spoke this great vidyā-mantra: "Tad dhana-pāgavadu-he."

By means of these expedient means, one establishes various ritual procedures; by performing them according to the Dharma, one achieves success as desired.
If a person, even while enjoying the pleasures of the five senses, constructs this maṇḍala, they shall achieve the fulfillment of all their wishes.

"Furthermore, these supreme secret methods of the Buddhas—the three types of samaya-heart-mantras, mudrās, signs, and so forth—should be transmitted to all disciples, and they should also be permitted to seek accomplishment according to their own inclinations."

When a disciple relies upon this secret ritual, they should arrange various subtle and exquisite offerings to the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and the ācārya, and with a sincere and earnest mind, seek all accomplishments.
"Whether performed by oneself or for another, it shall all be brought to completion.
He further expounded the supreme secret ritual of the Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajrapāṇi:

"The practitioner, following the original rite, should paint the Wrathful Vidyārāja, whose color is like the great sun-disk of vajra-fire, seated upon a multicolored lotus. On the left and right of the Vidyārāja atop the lotus, one should paint the four attendant Bodhisattvas:"
The first on the left is green, and the second is golden;
the first on the right is reddish-white, and the second is bluish-white.
Furthermore, four bodhisattvas are depicted on the left and right, each holding their respective insignia: the vajra-staff, the wheel, the bell, the banner, and so forth.
"Each shall assume an expression of joy or wrath and abide in their respective fundamental dharmas.
He then spoke the heart-mantra of that [deity]:

"HŪṂ (1) upahṛdaya-he (2). When the practitioner holds the vajra and bell in hand and recites this heart-mantra while installing the noble deities, the ritual for the completion of the image will be achieved.
Having thus arranged [the deities], the most supreme secret maṇḍala is thereby accomplished.
Thereafter, according to the ritual procedure, one should recite the samaya-mantra as follows: "HŪṂ TĀROGŪDHAVAKULADHA. (1)
